bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第129卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 129
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance — Volume 129

sentences.zh: 【宋紀十一】 起屠維大淵獻，盡閼逢執徐，凡六年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 11] — beginning in Tuxu Dayuanxian, ending in Efeng Zhixu, six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 11] From Tuxu Dayuanxian through Efeng Zhixu — six years in all.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝下大明三年（

translations.literal: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu, Continued — third year of Daming (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Continued — Third Year of Daming (

sentences.zh: 己亥，公元四五九年）

translations.literal: jihai, corresponding to the year 459 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: jihai, corresponding to 459 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己巳朔，兗州兵與魏皮豹子戰於高平，兗州兵不利。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jisi new moon, Yanzhou troops fought Pi Baozi of Wei at Gaoping; the Yanzhou troops were unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the jisi new moon of the first month, Yanzhou forces fought Pi Baozi of Northern Wei at Gaoping and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以驃騎將軍柳元景為尚作令，右僕射劉遵考為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On jichou, Rapid Cavalry General Liu Yuanjing was made Director of the Imperial Manufactories, and Right Vice Director Liu Zunkao was made Director of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Rapid Cavalry General Liu Yuanjing was appointed Director of the Imperial Manufactories, and Right Vice Director Liu Zunkao was appointed Director of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏河南公伊□卒。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Yi [character lost], Duke of Henan of Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Yi [name incomplete], Duke of Henan under Northern Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙卯，以揚州六郡為王畿，更以東揚州為揚州，徙治會稽，猶以星變故也。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yimao, the six commanderies of Yangzhou were made the royal domain; Eastern Yangzhou was renamed Yangzhou and the seat moved to Kuaiji — still because of celestial portents.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yimao, the six commanderies of Yangzhou were designated the royal domain; Eastern Yangzhou was renamed Yangzhou and the capital moved to Kuaiji — again on account of ominous stars.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚寅，以義興太守垣閬為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengyin, Yixing Administrator Yuan Lang was made Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengyin, Yixing Administrator Yuan Lang was appointed Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 閬，遵之子也。

translations.literal: Lang was the son of Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was Liu Zunkao's son.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙巳，魏主立其弟子推為京兆王。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, the Wei ruler enfeoffed his younger brother's son Tui as Prince of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on yisi, the Northern Wei emperor enfeoffed his younger brother's son Tui as Prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕知上意忌之，亦潛為之備；

translations.literal: Prince Jingling Liu Dan knew the emperor was suspicious of him and also secretly made preparations;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingling Liu Dan knew the emperor distrusted him and secretly made his own preparations as well;

sentences.zh: 因魏人入寇，修城浚隍，聚糧治仗。

translations.literal: because Wei forces invaded, he repaired the walls, dredged the moat, gathered grain, and readied weapons.
translations.idiomatic: when Northern Wei troops raided the borders, he repaired the walls, dredged the moat, stockpiled grain, and forged arms.

sentences.zh: 誕記室參軍江智淵知誕有異志，請假先還建康，上以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Dan's staff officer Jiang Zhiyuan, knowing Dan harbored a different intent, asked leave to return to Jiankang first; the emperor appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's registrar Jiang Zhiyuan, perceiving Dan's rebellious designs, asked leave to return to Jiankang ahead of the rest; the emperor appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 智淵，夷之弟子也，少有操行。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan was a nephew of Jiang Yi and from youth had integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan was a nephew of Jiang Yi and had shown moral discipline from an early age.

sentences.zh: 沈懷文每稱之曰：「人所應有盡有，人所應無盡無者，其唯江智淵乎！」

translations.literal: Shen Huaiwen often praised him, saying, "Of all that a man ought to have he has all; of all that a man ought not to have he has none — could it be anyone but Jiang Zhiyuan!"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen often said of him, "Everything a man should possess, he possesses; everything a man should not possess, he lacks — who else could it be but Jiang Zhiyuan!"

sentences.zh: 是時，道路皆雲誕反。

translations.literal: At this time, everyone on the roads said Dan was rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: By then rumor on every road had it that Liu Dan was plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 會吳郡民劉成上書稱：「息道龍昔事誕，見誕在石頭城修乘輿法物，習唱警蹕。

translations.literal: Then a man of Wu commandery, Liu Cheng, submitted a memorial saying, "My son Daolong once served Dan and saw Dan at Shitou City repairing imperial carriage regalia and practicing the cries of the imperial escort.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Cheng of Wu commandery memorialized the throne: "My son Daolong once served Liu Dan and saw him at Shitou City repairing imperial carriage regalia and drilling the cries of the imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 道龍憂懼，私與伴侶言之，誕殺道龍。」

translations.literal: Daolong was fearful and spoke of it privately to his companions; Dan killed Daolong."
translations.idiomatic: Daolong grew afraid and confided in his companions; Liu Dan had Daolong killed."

sentences.zh: 又豫章民陳談之上書稱：「弟詠之在誕左右，見誕疏陛下年紀姓諱，往巫鄭師憐家祝詛，詠之密以啟聞，誕誣言永之乘酒罵詈，殺之。」

translations.literal: Also a man of Yuzhang, Chen Tan, submitted a memorial saying, "My younger brother Yongzhi was at Dan's side and saw Dan write out Your Majesty's age and taboo name and send them to the shaman Zheng Shilian's household for curses; Yongzhi secretly reported this, and Dan falsely claimed Yongzhi had cursed him while drunk and killed him."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tan of Yuzhang also memorialized: "My brother Yongzhi served at Liu Dan's side and saw him write out Your Majesty's age and taboo name and send them to the shaman Zheng Shilian for curses; Yongzhi secretly informed the court, and Liu Dan falsely claimed Yongzhi had reviled him while drunk and put him to death."

sentences.zh: 上乃令有司奏誕罪惡，請收付廷尉治罪。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the relevant offices to memorialize Dan's crimes and request that he be taken into custody and tried by the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the relevant offices to present Liu Dan's crimes and request that he be arrested and tried by the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔貶誕爵為侯，遣之國。

translations.literal: On yimao, an edict degraded Dan's rank to marquis and sent him to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, an edict reduced Liu Dan to the rank of marquis and ordered him to his fief.

sentences.zh: 詔書未下，先以羽林禁兵配兗州刺史垣閬，使以之鎮為名。

translations.literal: Before the edict was issued, Palace Guard troops were first assigned to Yanzhou Governor Yuan Lang, under the pretext of proceeding to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict was even promulgated, Palace Guard troops were assigned to Yanzhou Governor Yuan Lang on the pretext that he was taking up his post.

sentences.zh: 與給事中戴明寶襲誕。

translations.literal: Together with Attendant Within the Palace Dai Mingbao he was to strike Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was to strike Liu Dan together with Attendant Within the Palace Dai Mingbao.

sentences.zh: 閬至廣陵，誕未悟也。

translations.literal: Lang reached Guangling; Dan had not yet realized what was happening.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lang reached Guangling, but Liu Dan still did not grasp what was afoot.

sentences.zh: 明寶夜報誕典簽蔣成，使明晨開門為內應。

translations.literal: Mingbao by night informed Dan's chief clerk Jiang Cheng to open the gate the next morning as an inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: That night Dai Mingbao notified Liu Dan's chief clerk Jiang Cheng to open the gates at dawn as an inside contact.

sentences.zh: 成以告府舍人許宗之，宗之入告誕；

translations.literal: Cheng told the household steward Xu Zongzhi; Zongzhi went in and informed Dan;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng told the household steward Xu Zongzhi, and Zongzhi went in to warn Liu Dan;

sentences.zh: 誕驚起，呼左右及素所畜養數百人執蔣成，勒兵自衛。

translations.literal: Dan started up in alarm, called his attendants and several hundred men he had long kept in his service to seize Jiang Cheng, and mustered troops to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan sprang up in alarm, summoned his attendants and several hundred retainers he had long kept on hand to seize Jiang Cheng, and mustered troops for his own defense.

sentences.zh: 天將曉，明寶與閬帥精兵數百人猝至，而門不開；

translations.literal: As dawn was breaking, Mingbao and Lang led several hundred picked troops in a sudden arrival, but the gate would not open;
translations.idiomatic: Just before dawn, Dai Mingbao and Yuan Lang led several hundred elite troops in a sudden assault, but the gates would not open;

sentences.zh: 誕已列兵登陴，自在門上斬蔣成，赦作徒、系囚，開門擊閬，殺之，明寶從間道逃還。

translations.literal: Dan had already drawn up his troops on the ramparts, personally beheaded Jiang Cheng on the gate tower, pardoned convict laborers and prisoners in bonds, opened the gate and struck Lang, killing him; Mingbao escaped by a hidden path.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan had already drawn up his men on the battlements, personally beheaded Jiang Cheng atop the gate tower, freed convict laborers and prisoners in bonds, opened the gates and struck Yuan Lang, killing him; Dai Mingbao fled back by a hidden path.

sentences.zh: 詔內外纂嚴。

translations.literal: An edict ordered strict security within and without.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered heightened security throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 以始興公沈慶之為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、南兗州刺史，將兵討誕。

translations.literal: Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou, and led troops to suppress Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou, and marched with an army to suppress Liu Dan.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上親總禁兵頓宣武堂。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the emperor personally took command of the Palace Guard and encamped at the Hall of Martial Display.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the emperor personally took command of the Palace Guard and encamped at the Hall of Martial Display.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史劉季之，誕故將也，素與都督宗愨有隙，聞誕反，恐為愨所害，委官，間道自歸朝廷。

translations.literal: Sizhou Governor Liu Jizhi was a former general of Dan's and had long been at odds with Commander Zong Que; hearing of Dan's rebellion, he feared Que would harm him, resigned his office, and by a hidden route returned to the court on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou Governor Liu Jizhi had once served under Liu Dan and long been at odds with Commander Zong Que; when he heard of the rebellion, fearing Que would destroy him, he resigned his post and made his way back to the court by hidden routes.

sentences.zh: 至盱眙，盱眙太守鄭瑗疑季之與誕同謀，邀殺之。

translations.literal: When he reached Xuyi, Xuyi Administrator Zheng Yuan suspected Jizhi was in league with Dan and waylaid and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuyi, Administrator Zheng Yuan suspected Liu Jizhi was in league with Liu Dan and ambushed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之至歐陽，誕遣慶之宗人沈道愍繼書說慶之，餉以玉環刀。

translations.literal: When Shen Qingzhi reached Ouyang, Dan sent Qingzhi's clansman Shen Daomin with a succession of letters to persuade Qingzhi and presented him with a jade-ring knife.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Qingzhi reached Ouyang, Liu Dan sent Qingzhi's kinsman Shen Daomin with letter after letter to win him over and presented him with a jade-ring knife.

sentences.zh: 慶之遣道愍返，數以罪惡。

translations.literal: Qingzhi sent Daomin back and enumerated Dan's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi sent Daomin back and laid out Liu Dan's crimes one by one.

sentences.zh: 誕焚郭邑，驅居民悉使入城，閉門自守，分遣書檄，邀結遠近，時山陽內史梁曠，家在廣陵，誕執其妻子，遣使邀曠，曠斬使拒之；

translations.literal: Dan burned the outer settlements, drove all the residents into the city, shut the gates and held his ground, and sent out proclamations far and wide to win allies; at that time Shanyang Interior Secretary Liang Kuang's family was in Guangling — Dan seized his wife and children and sent envoys to summon Kuang; Kuang beheaded the envoys and refused;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan burned the suburbs, drove every inhabitant into the city, shut the gates and held his ground, and sent proclamations far and wide to rally support; Shanyang Interior Secretary Liang Kuang's family was then in Guangling — Liu Dan seized his wife and children and sent envoys to summon him; Kuang beheaded the envoys and refused;

sentences.zh: 誕怒，滅其家。

translations.literal: Dan was enraged and exterminated his family.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan in his rage exterminated the entire family.

sentences.zh: 誕奉表投之城外曰：「陛下信用讒言，遂令無名小人來相掩襲；

translations.literal: Dan submitted a memorial and cast it outside the wall, saying, "Your Majesty has trusted slanderous words and thus sent nameless petty men to come and strike by surprise;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan submitted a memorial and cast it outside the wall: "Your Majesty has trusted slander and sent nameless petty men to strike by surprise;

sentences.zh: 不任枉酷，即加誅翦。

translations.literal: unable to bear wrongful cruelty, I have at once added execution and cutting down.
translations.idiomatic: unable to bear such wrongful cruelty, I have answered with execution and suppression.

sentences.zh: 雀鼠貪生，仰違詔敕。

translations.literal: Sparrows and mice crave life — I have turned my face upward against your edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Like sparrows and mice that cling to life, I have defied your edicts.

sentences.zh: 今親勒部曲，鎮扞徐、兗。

translations.literal: Now I personally lead my troops to garrison and defend Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Now I personally lead my troops to garrison and defend Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 先經何福，同生皇家？

translations.literal: What blessing did we receive before that we were born of the same royal house?
translations.idiomatic: What blessing did we once share, that we were born of the same royal house?

sentences.zh: 今有何愆，便成胡、越？

translations.literal: What offense do I have now that I have become as foreign as Hu and Yue?
translations.idiomatic: What offense have I committed now, that I have become as alien as barbarians of Hu and Yue?

sentences.zh: 陵鋒奮戈，萬沒豈顧；

translations.literal: With spear points raised and halberds brandished, ten thousand deaths I do not regard;
translations.idiomatic: With spear points raised and halberds brandished, I care nothing for ten thousand deaths;

sentences.zh: 蕩定之期，冀在旦夕。」

translations.literal: the day of pacification, I hope, lies within the morning and evening."
translations.idiomatic: the day of pacification, I trust, lies within the morning and evening."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下宮帷之丑，豈可三緘！」

translations.literal: He also said, "The ugliness within Your Majesty's palace curtains — how can it be sealed thrice!"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "The ugliness behind Your Majesty's palace curtains — how can it be sealed thrice over!"

sentences.zh: 上大怒，凡誕左右、腹心、同籍、期親在建康者並誅之，死者以千數，或有家人已死，方自城內出奔者。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged; all of Dan's attendants, confidants, those of the same household register, and close kin in Jiankang were executed together — the dead numbered in the thousands — and some whose families were already dead were only then fleeing from within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage; every attendant, confidant, clansman, and close kinsman of Liu Dan in Jiankang was put to death — the slain numbered in the thousands — and some whose families were already dead were only then fleeing from within the city.

sentences.zh: 慶之至城下，誕登樓謂之曰：「沈公垂白之年，何苦來此！」

translations.literal: When Qingzhi reached below the wall, Dan mounted the tower and said to him, "Lord Shen, in the years when your hair hangs white — why trouble yourself to come here!"
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhi reached the foot of the wall, Liu Dan mounted the tower and called down, "Lord Shen, in the years when your hair has turned white — why trouble yourself to come here!"

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「朝廷以君狂愚，不足勞少壯故耳。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said, "The court considered you mad and foolish — not worth troubling the young and strong, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi replied, "The court judged you mad and foolish — not worth troubling the young and strong, that is all."

sentences.zh: 上慮誕奔魏，使慶之斷其走路。

translations.literal: The emperor feared Dan would flee to Wei and ordered Qingzhi to cut off his escape route.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared Liu Dan would flee to Northern Wei and ordered Qingzhi to cut off his escape routes.

sentences.zh: 慶之移營白土，去城十八里，又進軍新亭。

translations.literal: Qingzhi moved camp to Baitu, eighteen li from the city, and then advanced the army to Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi moved camp to Baitu, eighteen li from the city, then advanced to Xinting.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史宗愨、徐州刺史劉道隆並帥眾來會；

translations.literal: Yuzhou Governor Zong Que and Xuzhou Governor Liu Daolong both led their forces to join him;
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou Governor Zong Que and Xuzhou Governor Liu Daolong both led their forces to join him;

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史沈僧明，慶之兄子也，亦遣兵助慶之。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Governor Shen Sengming, Qingzhi's elder brother's son, also sent troops to aid Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou Governor Shen Sengming, Qingzhi's nephew, also sent troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 先是誕誑其眾，云「宗愨助我」；

translations.literal: Earlier Dan had deceived his troops, saying, "Zong Que is helping me";
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Dan had deceived his troops, saying, "Zong Que is on my side";

sentences.zh: 愨至，繞城曜馬呼曰：「我，宗愨也！」

translations.literal: when Que arrived, he circled the city displaying his horse and shouted, "It is I, Zong Que!"
translations.idiomatic: when Que arrived, he rode around the city displaying his mount and shouted, "It is I, Zong Que!"

sentences.zh: 誕見眾軍大集，欲棄城北走，留中兵參軍申靈賜守廣陵，自將步騎數百人，親信並自隨，聲雲出戰，邪趨海陵道。

translations.literal: Dan, seeing the mass of armies gathered, wished to abandon the city and flee north; he left Central Troops Staff Officer Shen Lingci to hold Guangling, personally led several hundred infantry and cavalry with his close confidants following him, claiming he was going out to fight while slanting toward the Hailing road.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the armies massed against him, Liu Dan wished to abandon the city and flee north; he left Central Troops Staff Officer Shen Lingci to hold Guangling, personally led several hundred foot and horse with his closest confidants in train, claiming he was going out to fight while veering toward the Hailing road.

sentences.zh: 慶之遣龍驤將軍武念追之。

translations.literal: Qingzhi sent Dragon Cavalry General Wu Nian in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi sent Dragon Cavalry General Wu Nian in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 誕行十餘里，眾皆不欲去，互請誕還城。

translations.literal: After Dan had gone more than ten li, none of his followers wished to leave, and they repeatedly asked Dan to return to the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Dan had gone more than ten li, none of his followers wished to leave, and they repeatedly begged him to return to the city.

sentences.zh: 誕曰：「我還易耳，卿能為我盡力乎？」

translations.literal: Dan said, "My return is easy — can you all exert yourselves on my behalf?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan said, "Returning is easy for me — but will you all fight your hardest for me?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆許諾，誕乃復還，築壇歃血以誓眾，凡府州文武皆加秩。

translations.literal: All promised, and Dan then returned; he built an altar, drank blood in oath to bind the host, and promoted every civil and military officer of the prefecture and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: All promised, and Liu Dan turned back; he built an altar, drank blood in oath to bind his followers, and promoted every civil and military officer of the prefecture and commandery.

sentences.zh: 以主簿劉琨之為中兵參軍；

translations.literal: He made chief clerk Liu Kunzhi Central Troops Staff Officer;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed chief clerk Liu Kunzhi Central Troops Staff Officer;

sentences.zh: 琨之，遵考之子也，辭曰：「忠孝不得並。

translations.literal: Kunzhi was the son of Zunkao and declined, saying, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot stand together.
translations.idiomatic: Kunzhi was Liu Zunkao's son and declined, saying, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot stand together.

sentences.zh: 琨之老父在，不敢承命。」

translations.literal: Kunzhi's aged father is alive — I dare not accept the commission."
translations.idiomatic: My aged father is still alive — I dare not accept the commission."

sentences.zh: 誕囚之十餘日，終不受，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Dan imprisoned him for more than ten days; he still would not accept, and Dan then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan imprisoned him for more than ten days; when he still refused, Liu Dan had him killed.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍垣護之、虎賁中郎將殷孝祖等擊魏還，至廣陵，上並使受慶之節度。

translations.literal: Right Guard General Yuan Huzhi, Tiger Guard Commandant Yin Xiaozu, and others, returning from striking Wei, reached Guangling; the emperor ordered them all to accept Qingzhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Yuan Huzhi, Tiger Guard Commandant Yin Xiaozu, and others, returning from campaigns against Northern Wei, reached Guangling; the emperor placed them all under Qingzhi's command.

sentences.zh: 慶之進營，逼廣陵城。

translations.literal: Qingzhi advanced camp and pressed upon Guangling city.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi advanced his camp and pressed close to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 誕餉慶之食，提挈者百餘人，出自北門；

translations.literal: Dan sent food to Qingzhi; more than a hundred bearers came out from the north gate;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan sent food to Qingzhi; more than a hundred bearers came out through the north gate;

sentences.zh: 慶之不開視，悉焚之。

translations.literal: Qingzhi would not look and burned it all.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi would not even look and had it all burned.

sentences.zh: 誕於城上授函表，請慶之為送，慶之曰：「我受詔討賊，不得為汝送表。

translations.literal: Dan handed down a sealed memorial from atop the wall and asked Qingzhi to deliver it; Qingzhi said, "I have received orders to suppress the rebel — I cannot deliver your memorial for you.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan handed down a sealed memorial from atop the wall and asked Qingzhi to deliver it; Qingzhi said, "I have orders to suppress the rebel — I cannot carry your memorial for you.

sentences.zh: 汝必欲歸死朝廷，自應開門遣使，吾為汝護送。」

translations.literal: If you truly wish to return and die before the court, you should yourself open the gate and send envoys — I will escort them for you."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly wish to surrender and die before the court, open the gates yourself and send envoys — I will escort them for you."

sentences.zh: 東揚州刺史顏竣遭母憂，送喪還都，上恩待猶厚，竣時對親舊有怨言，或語及朝廷得失。

translations.literal: Eastern Yangzhou Governor Yan Jun, having suffered his mother's death, escorted the funeral back to the capital; the emperor's favor toward him was still generous, but Jun at times voiced complaints to kin and old friends, sometimes speaking of the court's right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yangzhou Governor Yan Jun, in mourning for his mother, escorted her funeral back to the capital; the emperor still treated him generously, but Jun at times complained to kin and old friends, sometimes touching on the court's failings.

sentences.zh: 會王僧達得罪，疑竣譖之；

translations.literal: When Wang Sengda fell afoul of the law, he suspected Jun had slandered him;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengda fell from favor, he suspected Yan Jun had slandered him;

sentences.zh: 將死，具陳竣前後怨望誹謗之語。

translations.literal: facing death, he fully set forth all of Jun's words of resentment, complaint, and slander before and after.
translations.idiomatic: facing execution, he laid out in full every resentful and slanderous remark Yan Jun had made.

sentences.zh: 上乃使御史中丞庾微之劾奏，免竣官。

translations.literal: The emperor then had Imperial Censor Yu Weizhi memorialize accusations and dismiss Jun from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Imperial Censor Yu Weizhi memorialize accusations and strip Yan Jun of his office.

sentences.zh: 竣愈懼，上啟陳謝，且請生命；

translations.literal: Jun grew still more fearful, submitted a memorial expressing regret, and also begged for his life;
translations.idiomatic: Jun grew still more fearful, submitted a memorial of apology, and begged for his life;

sentences.zh: 上益怒，詔答曰：「卿訕訐怨憤，已孤本望；

translations.literal: the emperor grew angrier still and replied by edict, "Your mockery, accusations, resentment, and anger have already betrayed my hopes;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor grew angrier still and replied by edict, "Your mockery, accusations, and resentment have already betrayed my hopes;

sentences.zh: 乃復過煩思慮，懼不自全，豈為下事上誠節之至邪！」

translations.literal: yet you again trouble me with your anxious thoughts, fearing you cannot preserve yourself — is this the utmost sincerity and integrity of a subject serving his lord!"
translations.idiomatic: yet you trouble me again with your anxious fears for your own safety — is this the utmost sincerity of a subject serving his lord!"

sentences.zh: 及竟陵王誕反，上遂誣竣與誕通謀，五月，收竣付廷尉，先折其足，然後賜死。

translations.literal: When Prince Jingling Liu Dan rebelled, the emperor then falsely charged Jun with plotting together with Dan; in the fifth month, Jun was taken into custody and handed to the Court of Justice — first his legs were broken, then he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jingling Liu Dan rebelled, the emperor then falsely charged Yan Jun with plotting alongside him; in the fifth month, Jun was arrested and handed to the Court of Justice — his legs were broken first, then he was granted death.

sentences.zh: 妻子徙交州，至宮亭湖，復沉其男口。

translations.literal: His wife and children were banished to Jiaozhou; at Gongting Lake, his sons were again drowned.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children were banished to Jiaozhou; at Gongting Lake, his sons were drowned as well.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wushen, the Wei ruler went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wushen, the Northern Wei emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 上命沈慶之為三烽於桑裡，若克外城，舉一烽，克內城，舉兩烽，擒劉誕，舉三烽；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shen Qingzhi to set up three beacon fires at Sangli: if the outer city were taken, raise one beacon; if the inner city were taken, raise two; if Liu Dan were captured, raise three;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Shen Qingzhi to set up three beacon fires at Sangli: one beacon if the outer city fell, two if the inner city fell, three if Liu Dan were captured;

sentences.zh: 璽書督趣，前後相繼。

translations.literal: imperial letters pressed him on, one after another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: imperial letters pressing him onward arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 慶之焚其東門，塞塹，造攻道，立行樓、土山並諸攻具，值久雨，不得攻城。

translations.literal: Qingzhi burned the east gate, filled the moat, constructed assault ramps, erected mobile towers and earthen mounds and all manner of siege engines — but prolonged rain prevented assault on the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi burned the east gate, filled the moat, built assault ramps, erected mobile towers and earthen mounds and every sort of siege engine — but weeks of rain prevented any assault on the city.

sentences.zh: 上使御史中丞庾微之奏免慶之官，詔勿問，以激之。

translations.literal: The emperor had Imperial Censor Yu Weizhi memorialize a request to dismiss Qingzhi from office; an edict said not to inquire — to spur him on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Imperial Censor Yu Weizhi memorialize a request to dismiss Qingzhi from office; an edict declined to act — to spur him on.

sentences.zh: 自四月至於秋七月，雨止，城猶未拔。

translations.literal: From the fourth month until the seventh month of autumn the rain ceased, yet the city had still not been taken.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth month until the seventh month of autumn the rain ceased, yet the city still had not fallen.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命太史擇日，將自濟江討誕；

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, ordered the Grand Astrologer to choose a day, and was about to cross the river himself to suppress Dan;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in his rage ordered the Grand Astrologer to choose a day and prepared to cross the Yangzi himself to suppress Liu Dan;

sentences.zh: 太宰義恭固諫。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yigong firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Liu Yigong firmly remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 誕初閉城拒使者，記室參軍山陰賀弼固諫，誕怒，抽刀向之，乃止。

translations.literal: When Dan first shut the city and refused the envoys, his staff officer He Bi of Shanyin firmly remonstrated; Dan was enraged, drew his blade toward him, and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Dan first shut the city and refused the envoys, his registrar He Bi of Shanyin firmly remonstrated; Liu Dan in his rage drew his blade on him, then stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 誕遣兵出戰，屢敗，將佐多逾城出降。

translations.literal: Dan sent troops out to fight and was repeatedly defeated; many officers and aides climbed over the wall to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan sent troops out to fight and was repeatedly defeated; many officers and aides climbed over the wall to surrender.

sentences.zh: 或勸弼宜早出，弼曰：「公舉兵向朝廷，此事既不可從；

translations.literal: Some urged Bi that he ought to leave early; Bi said, "The lord has raised troops against the court — this matter I cannot follow;
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Bi to leave while he still could; Bi said, "Our lord has raised troops against the court — that I cannot follow;

sentences.zh: 荷公厚恩，又義無違背，唯當以死明心耳！」

translations.literal: yet I have received the lord's deep grace, and in righteousness I cannot betray him — I can only make my heart clear through death!"
translations.idiomatic: yet I have received his deep grace, and in righteousness I cannot betray him — I can only make my loyalty clear through death!"

sentences.zh: 乃飲藥自殺。

translations.literal: He then drank poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then took poison and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 參軍何康之等謀開門納官軍，不果，斬關出降。

translations.literal: Staff Officer He Kangzhi and others plotted to open the gate and admit the government army; it did not succeed, and they cut through the barrier and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer He Kangzhi and others plotted to open the gates and admit the imperial army; the plot failed, and they cut through the barrier and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 誕為高樓，置康之母於其上，暴露之，不與食；

translations.literal: Dan built a high tower, placed Kang's mother atop it, exposed her to the elements, and gave her no food;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan built a high tower, placed He Kang's mother atop it, exposed her to the elements, and gave her no food;

sentences.zh: 母呼康之，數日而死。

translations.literal: the mother called for Kangzhi, and after several days died.
translations.idiomatic: she called for Kangzhi day after day, and after several days died.

sentences.zh: 誕以中軍長濟陽范義為左司馬。

translations.literal: Dan made Central Army Chief Fan Yi of Jiyang Left Staff Major.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan appointed Central Army Chief Fan Yi of Jiyang as Left Staff Major.

sentences.zh: 義母妻子皆在城內，或謂義曰：「事必不振，子其行乎！」

translations.literal: Yi's mother, wife, and children were all within the city; some said to Yi, "The affair surely cannot succeed — will you not leave?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi's mother, wife, and children were all inside the city; some urged him, "This cause cannot succeed — you should leave while you can!"

sentences.zh: 義曰：「吾，人吏也；

translations.literal: Yi said, "I am a man who serves as an officer;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi replied, "I am a man who serves as an officer;

sentences.zh: 子不可以棄母，吏不可以叛君。

translations.literal: a son cannot abandon his mother, and an officer cannot betray his lord.
translations.idiomatic: a son cannot abandon his mother, and an officer cannot betray his lord.

sentences.zh: 必若何康之而活，吾弗為也。」

translations.literal: If I must live as He Kangzhi did, I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: If I must live as He Kangzhi did, I will not do it."

sentences.zh: 沈慶之帥眾攻城，身先士卒，親犯矢石，乙巳，克其外城；

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi led the host in assault on the city, himself going before the soldiers and personally braving arrows and stones; on yisi he took the outer city;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi led the assault on the city, himself going before the troops and braving arrows and stones in person; on yisi he took the outer city;

sentences.zh: 乘勝而進，又克小城。

translations.literal: pressing the victory forward, he also took the inner ward.
translations.idiomatic: pressing the victory forward, he also took the inner ward.

sentences.zh: 誕聞兵入，走趨後園，隊主沈胤之等追及之，擊傷誕，墜水，引出，斬之。

translations.literal: Dan, hearing troops had entered, ran toward the rear garden; squad leader Shen Yinzhi and others overtook him, struck and wounded Dan, he fell into the water, was pulled out, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing troops had broken in, Liu Dan fled toward the rear garden; squad leader Shen Yinzhi and others overtook him, wounded him, he fell into the water, was pulled out, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 誕母、妻皆自殺。

translations.literal: Dan's mother and wife both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan's mother and wife both killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 上聞廣陵平，出宣陽門，敕左右皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing Guangling was pacified, went out the Xuanyang Gate and ordered those at his side all to cry "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Guangling had fallen, the emperor went out the Xuanyang Gate and ordered everyone at his side to cry "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 侍中蔡興宗陪輦，上顧曰：「卿何獨不呼？」

translations.literal: Attendant Within Cai Xingzong accompanied the carriage; the emperor turned and said, "Why do you alone not cry out?"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Within Cai Xingzong rode beside the carriage; the emperor turned and said, "Why do you alone not shout?"

sentences.zh: 興宗正色曰：「陛下今日正應涕泣行誅，豈得皆稱萬歲！」

translations.literal: Xingzong said with a stern countenance, "Your Majesty today ought rather to weep tears and carry out executions — how can all cry 'Ten thousand years'!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said gravely, "Your Majesty today ought rather to weep and carry out executions — how can everyone shout 'Long live the emperor'!"

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 詔貶誕姓留氏，廣陵城中士民，無大小悉命殺之。

translations.literal: An edict degraded Dan's surname to Liu; within Guangling city, commoners and gentry, none great or small, were all ordered killed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict degraded Liu Dan's clan to the surname Liu; every man, woman, and child in Guangling was ordered put to death.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之請自五尺以下全之，其餘男子皆死，女子以為軍賞；

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi requested that those below five chi be spared; all other males were to die, and women were to be given as military rewards;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi pleaded that those below five chi in height be spared; all other males were to die, and the women were to be given as military rewards;

sentences.zh: 猶殺三千餘口。

translations.literal: still more than three thousand persons were killed.
translations.idiomatic: still more than three thousand people were killed.

sentences.zh: 長水校尉宗越臨決，皆先刳腸抉眼，或笞面鞭腹，苦酒灌創，然後斬之，越對之，欣欣若有所得。

translations.literal: Chief of the Changshui Guard Zong Yue presided over the executions; all were first disemboweled and their eyes gouged out, or flogged on the face and whipped on the belly, strong wine poured into the wounds, and then beheaded — Yue faced this with delight, as if he had gained something.
translations.idiomatic: Chief of the Changshui Guard Zong Yue presided over the executions; each victim was first disemboweled and blinded, or flogged on the face and whipped on the belly, strong wine poured into the wounds, and then beheaded — Yue watched with delight, as if he had gained something.

sentences.zh: 上聚其首於石頭南岸為京觀，侍中沈懷文諫，不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor gathered their heads on the south bank of Shitou to make a victory mound; Attendant Within Shen Huaiwen remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor piled their heads on the south bank of Shitou into a victory mound; Attendant Within Shen Huaiwen remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 初，誕自知將敗，使黃門呂曇濟與左右素所信者將世子景粹匿於民間，謂曰：「事若不濟，思相全脫；

translations.literal: Earlier, Dan, knowing he would be defeated, sent Yellow Gate Lü Yanji with those he had long trusted to hide his heir Jingcui among the common people, saying, "If the affair does not succeed, think how to preserve and deliver him;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, knowing he would be defeated, Liu Dan sent Yellow Gate Lü Yanji with his most trusted men to hide his heir Jingcui among the common people, saying, "If things fail, find a way to save him;

sentences.zh: 如其不免，可深埋之。」

translations.literal: if he cannot be spared, you may bury him deep."
translations.idiomatic: if he cannot be spared, bury him deep."

sentences.zh: 各分以金寶繼送。

translations.literal: Each was given gold and jewels in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Each was given gold and jewels in turn.

sentences.zh: 既出門，並散走；

translations.literal: Once they had left the gate, all scattered and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Once outside the gates, all scattered and fled;

sentences.zh: 唯曇濟不去，攜負景粹十餘日，捕得，斬之。

translations.literal: only Yanji did not leave, carrying Jingcui on his back for more than ten days; they were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: only Yanji did not leave, carrying Jingcui on his back for more than ten days until they were captured and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 臨川內史羊璿坐與誕素善，下獄死。

translations.literal: Linchuan Interior Secretary Yang Xuan was charged with having long been on good terms with Dan, imprisoned, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Linchuan Interior Secretary Yang Xuan, charged with having long been close to Liu Dan, was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 擢梁曠為後將軍，贈劉琨之給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Liang Kuang was promoted to Rear General; Liu Kunzhi was posthumously given Attendant Within the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kuang was promoted to Rear General; Liu Kunzhi was posthumously appointed Attendant Within the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗奉旨慰勞廣陵。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong received orders to comfort and reward Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong received orders to comfort and reward Guangling.

sentences.zh: 興宗與范義素善，收斂其屍，送喪歸豫章。

translations.literal: Xingzong had long been on good terms with Fan Yi; he gathered Yi's corpse and sent the funeral back to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong had long been close to Fan Yi; he gathered Yi's corpse and sent the funeral back to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「卿何敢故觸王憲？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "How dare you deliberately offend the royal statutes?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "How dare you deliberately defy the royal statutes?"

sentences.zh: 興宗抗言對曰：「陛下自殺賊，臣自葬故交，何不可之有！」

translations.literal: Xingzong answered defiantly, "Your Majesty kills rebels yourself; I bury an old friend myself — what is not permitted in that!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong answered boldly, "Your Majesty kills rebels; I bury an old friend — what is wrong with that!"

sentences.zh: 上有慚色。

translations.literal: The emperor showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 宗越治軍嚴，善為營陳。

translations.literal: Zong Yue governed the army strictly and was skilled at arranging encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yue governed the army with strict discipline and was skilled at arranging encampments.

sentences.zh: 每數萬人止頓，越自騎馬前行，使軍人隨其後，馬止營合，未嘗參差。

translations.literal: Whenever tens of thousands halted, Yue himself rode ahead on horseback and had the soldiers follow behind; when the horse stopped, the camp aligned — never once out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever tens of thousands halted, Yue rode ahead on horseback while the soldiers followed behind; when his horse stopped, the camp aligned — never once out of order.

sentences.zh: 辛未，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinwei, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以丹陽尹劉秀之為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Danyang Prefect Liu Xiuzhi was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Danyang Prefect Liu Xiuzhi was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以南兗州刺史沈慶之為司空，刺史如故。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Southern Yanzhou Governor Shen Qingzhi was made Minister of Works, his governorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Southern Yanzhou Governor Shen Qingzhi was appointed Minister of Works while retaining his governorship.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，魏主如雲中；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengxu, the Wei ruler went to Yunzhong;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengxu, the Northern Wei emperor went to Yunzhong;

sentences.zh: 壬戌，還平城。

translations.literal: on renxu, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: on renxu, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬辰，築上林苑於玄武湖北。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renchen, the Upper Forest Park was built north of Xuanwu Lake.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renchen, the Upper Forest Park was built north of Xuanwu Lake.

sentences.zh: 初，晉人築南郊壇於巳位，尚書右丞徐爰以為非禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jin people had built the southern suburban altar in the si position; Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat Xu Ai held this contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Jin had built the southern suburban altar in the si position; Right Assistant Director Xu Ai held this contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 詔徙於牛頭山西，直宮城之午位。

translations.literal: An edict moved it west of Niutou Mountain, directly aligned with the palace city's wu position.
translations.idiomatic: An edict moved it west of Niutou Mountain, directly aligned with the palace city's south-facing position.

sentences.zh: 及廢帝即位，以舊地為吉，復還故處。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, the old site was considered auspicious and it was moved back to the former place.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, the old site was considered auspicious and the altar was moved back.

sentences.zh: 帝又命尚書左丞荀萬秋造五路，依金根車，加羽葆蓋。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Left Assistant Director Xun Wanqiu to make five imperial carriages, modeled on the golden-root carriage, with feather canopies added.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Left Assistant Director Xun Wanqiu to build five imperial carriages modeled on the golden-root carriage, with feather canopies added.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝下大明四年（

translations.literal: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu, Continued — fourth year of Daming (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Continued — Fourth Year of Daming (

sentences.zh: 庚子，公元四六零年）

translations.literal: gengzi, corresponding to the year 460 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: gengzi, corresponding to 460 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲子朔，魏大赦，改元和平。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jiazi new moon, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Heping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the jiazi new moon of the first month, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Heping (Peace).

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上耕籍田，大赦。

translations.literal: On yihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔祀郊廟，初乘玉路。

translations.literal: On jimao, an edict ordered sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; for the first time the jade carriage was used.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, an edict ordered sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; for the first time the jade imperial carriage was used.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，立皇子子勳為晉安王，子房為尋陽王，子頊為歷陽王，子鸞為襄陽王。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the princes Zixun was made Prince of Jin'an, Zifang Prince of Xunyang, Zixu Prince of Liyang, and Ziluan Prince of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Prince Zixun was made Prince of Jin'an, Zifang Prince of Xunyang, Zixu Prince of Liyang, and Ziluan Prince of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 魏散騎侍郎馮闡來聘。

translations.literal: Feng Chan, Attendant Cavalier of Wei, came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Chan, Attendant Cavalier of Northern Wei, came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏衛將軍樂安王良討河西叛胡。

translations.literal: In the second month, Wei Guard General Prince Liang of Le'an suppressed the rebel Hu of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Northern Wei Guard General Prince Liang of Le'an suppressed the rebel Hu of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏人寇北陰平，朱提太守楊歸子擊破之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wei forces raided Beiyinping; Zhuti Administrator Yang Guizi defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Northern Wei forces raided Beiyinping; Zhuti Administrator Yang Guizi defeated them.

sentences.zh: 甲申，皇后親桑於西郊，皇太后觀禮。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the empress personally tended the mulberry trees at the western suburb; the empress dowager observed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the empress personally tended the mulberry trees at the western suburb while the empress dowager observed the rite.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，魏太后常氏殂。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Empress Dowager Chang of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Empress Dowager Chang of Northern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸丑，魏葬昭太后於鳴雞山。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guichou, Wei buried Empress Dowager Zhao on Mingji Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guichou, Northern Wei buried Empress Dowager Zhao on Mingji Mountain.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，尚書左僕射褚湛之卒。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Chu Zhanzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Left Vice Director Chu Zhanzhi died.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王拾寅兩受宋、魏爵命，居止出入，擬於王者，魏人忿之。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun King Shiyin had twice received enfeoffment from both Song and Wei; his dwelling, comings and goings were patterned on a king's — the Wei people resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun King Shiyin had accepted enfeoffment from both Song and Northern Wei; his dwelling and comings and goings were patterned on a king's — the Wei court resented this.

sentences.zh: 定陽侯曹安表：「拾寅今保白蘭，若分軍出其左右，必走保南山，不過十日，人畜乏食，可一舉而定。」

translations.literal: Marquis of Dingyang Cao An memorialized, "Shiyin now holds Bailan; if we divide the army to emerge on his left and right, he will surely flee to hold the southern mountains — within ten days men and livestock will lack food, and he can be settled in one stroke."
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Dingyang Cao An memorialized, "Shiyin now holds Bailan; if we divide our forces to strike on both flanks, he will surely flee to the southern mountains — within ten days his men and livestock will starve, and we can settle him in one stroke."

sentences.zh: 六月，甲午，魏遣征西大將軍陽平王新成等督統萬、高平諸軍出南道，南郡公中山李惠等督涼州諸軍出北道，以擊吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiawu, Wei sent Campaign-west Grand General Prince Xincheng of Yangping and others to command the armies of Wan and Gaoping on the southern route, and Duke of Zhongshan Li Hui of Nan commandery and others to command the armies of Liangzhou on the northern route, to strike Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiawu, Northern Wei sent Campaign-west Grand General Prince Xincheng of Yangping to command the Wan and Gaoping armies on the southern route, and Duke of Zhongshan Li Hui to command the Liangzhou armies on the northern route, to strike Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 魏崔浩之誅也，史官遂廢，至是復置。

translations.literal: When Cui Hao of Wei was executed, the historiographical office was then abolished; at this time it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hao of Northern Wei was executed, the historiographical office had been abolished; now it was restored.

sentences.zh: 河西叛胡詣長安首罪，魏遣使者安慰之。

translations.literal: The rebel Hu of Hexi came to Chang'an to confess their crimes; Wei sent envoys to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Hu of Hexi came to Chang'an to confess their crimes; Northern Wei sent envoys to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，遣使如魏。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, envoys were sent to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, envoys were sent to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，開府儀同三司何尚之卒。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon He Shangzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon He Shangzhi died.

sentences.zh: 壬午，魏主如河西。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Wei ruler went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the Northern Wei emperor went to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 魏軍至西平，吐谷渾王拾寅走保南山。

translations.literal: Wei forces reached Xiping; Tuyuhun King Shiyin fled to hold the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei forces reached Xiping; Tuyuhun King Shiyin fled to the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 九月，魏軍濟河追之，會疾疫，引還，獲雜畜二十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wei forces crossed the river in pursuit; encountering epidemic disease, they withdrew, capturing more than two hundred thousand head of miscellaneous livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Northern Wei forces crossed the river in pursuit; when epidemic disease broke out, they withdrew, capturing more than two hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，徒襄陽王子鸞為新安王。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Prince Ziluan of Xiangyang was moved to be Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Prince Ziluan of Xiangyang was transferred to be Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 十月，庚寅，詔沈慶之討緣江蠻。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on gengyin, an edict ordered Shen Qingzhi to suppress the river-bank barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on gengyin, an edict ordered Shen Qingzhi to suppress the barbarians along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 前廬陵內史周郎，言事切直，上銜之。

translations.literal: Former Linling Interior Secretary Zhou Lang spoke on affairs with blunt directness; the emperor bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Former Linling Interior Secretary Zhou Lang spoke bluntly on state affairs; the emperor bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 使有司奏郎居母喪不如禮，傳送寧州，於道殺之。

translations.literal: He had the relevant offices memorialize that Lang, during mourning for his mother, had not observed ritual propriety; Lang was sent in custody to Ningzhou and killed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He had the relevant offices charge that Lang had not observed mourning ritual properly for his mother; Lang was sent in custody to Ningzhou and killed on the road.

sentences.zh: 朗之行也，侍中蔡興宗方在直，請與朗別；

translations.literal: When Lang was departing, Attendant Within Cai Xingzong was then on palace duty and asked to take leave of Lang;
translations.idiomatic: When Lang was being sent away, Attendant Within Cai Xingzong was on palace duty and asked to bid him farewell;

sentences.zh: 坐白衣領職。

translations.literal: he was punished by wearing white and retaining his post.
translations.idiomatic: he was punished by being required to wear white while retaining his post.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏散騎侍郎盧度世等來聘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Lu Dushi and others, Attendant Cavalier of Wei, came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Lu Dushi and others, Attendant Cavalier of Northern Wei, came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上征青、冀二州刺史顏師伯為侍中。

translations.literal: This year, the emperor summoned Qing and Ji Governors Yan Shibo to be Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: This year, the emperor summoned Qing and Ji Governors Yan Shibo to court as Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 師伯以諂佞被親任，群臣莫及，多納貨賄，家累千金。

translations.literal: Shibo, through flattery and sycophancy, won intimate trust; no minister could match him; he accepted many bribes, and his household amassed thousands in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo won the emperor's intimate trust through flattery and sycophancy; no minister could match him; he accepted many bribes, and his household amassed great wealth.

sentences.zh: 上嘗與之樗蒲，上擲得雉，自謂必勝；

translations.literal: The emperor once played pitch-pot with him; the emperor threw and got a pheasant, and declared himself certain to win;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once played pitch-pot with him; the emperor threw and got a pheasant, and declared himself certain to win;

sentences.zh: 師伯次擲，得盧，上失色。

translations.literal: Shibo threw next and got a deer; the emperor's face fell.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo threw next and got a deer; the emperor's face fell.

sentences.zh: 師伯遽斂子曰：「幾作盧！」

translations.literal: Shibo quickly gathered the dice and said, "I nearly made a deer!"
translations.idiomatic: Shibo quickly gathered the dice and exclaimed, "I nearly made a deer!"

sentences.zh: 是日，師伯一輸百萬。

translations.literal: That day Shibo lost a million in one throw.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shibo deliberately lost a million in one throw.

sentences.zh: 柔然攻高昌，殺沮渠安周，滅沮渠氏，以闞伯周為高昌王。

translations.literal: Rouran attacked Gaochang, killed Juqu Anzhou, extinguished the Juqu clan, and made Kan Bozhou King of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran attacked Gaochang, killed Juqu Anzhou, extinguished the Juqu clan, and made Kan Bozhou King of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 高昌稱王自此始。

translations.literal: Gaochang's assumption of kingship began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this Gaochang began to claim kingship.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝下大明五年（

translations.literal: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu, Continued — fifth year of Daming (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Continued — Fifth Year of Daming (

sentences.zh: 辛丑，公元四六一年）

translations.literal: xinchou, corresponding to the year 461 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: xinchou, corresponding to 461 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊午朔，朝賀。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the wuwu new moon, court congratulations were held.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the wuwu new moon of the first month, the court held its New Year audience.

sentences.zh: 雪落太宰義恭衣，有六出，義恭奏以為瑞，上悅。

translations.literal: Snow fell on Grand Tutor Yigong's robe with six-pointed flakes; Yigong memorialized that this was an auspicious sign, and the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell on Grand Tutor Liu Yigong's robe in six-pointed flakes; Yigong memorialized that this was an auspicious sign, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 義恭以上猜暴，懼不自容，每卑辭遜色，曲意祗奉；

translations.literal: Yigong, because the emperor was suspicious and violent, feared he could not preserve himself and always used humble words and yielding countenance, bending his will in respectful service;
translations.idiomatic: Yigong, knowing the emperor was suspicious and violent, feared for his life and always spoke humbly and deferentially, bending every effort to please him;

sentences.zh: 由是終上之世，得免於禍。

translations.literal: thereby through the emperor's entire reign he escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: and so through the emperor's entire reign he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，魏主如中山；

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinmao, the Wei ruler went to Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao, the Northern Wei emperor went to Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 丙午，至鄴，遂如信都。

translations.literal: on bingwu he reached Ye, then went on to Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: on bingwu he reached Ye, then went on to Xindu.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣使如魏。

translations.literal: In the third month, envoys were sent to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, envoys were sent to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主發並、肆州民五千人治河西獵道；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler mobilized five thousand people from Bing and Xi provinces to repair the hunting roads of Hexi;
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor mobilized five thousand people from Bing and Xi provinces to repair the hunting roads of Hexi;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，還平城。

translations.literal: on xinsi he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: on xinsi he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸巳，更以西陽王子尚為豫章王。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guisi, Prince Zishang of Xiyang was again made Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on guisi, Prince Zishang of Xiyang was again made Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔經始明堂，直作大殿於丙、己之地，制如太廟，唯十有二間為異。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict ordered the commencement of the Bright Hall; a great hall was to be built directly in the bing and ji positions, its form like the Imperial Ancestral Temple, differing only in having twelve bays.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, an edict ordered construction of the Bright Hall; a great hall was to be built in the bing and ji positions, modeled on the Imperial Ancestral Temple but with twelve bays.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史海陵王休茂，年十七，司馬新野庾深之行府事。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Governor Prince Xiumao of Hailing, seventeen years old — his staff major Yu Shenzhi of Xinye conducted the prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou Governor Prince Xiumao of Hailing was seventeen; his staff major Yu Shenzhi of Xinye conducted the prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 休茂性急，欲自專處決，深之及主帥每禁之，常懷忿恨。

translations.literal: Xiumao's nature was impatient; he wished to decide matters on his own authority — Shenzhi and the commandant repeatedly restrained him, and he constantly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiumao was impatient by nature and wished to decide everything himself — Shenzhi and the commandant repeatedly restrained him, and he constantly nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 左右張伯超有寵，多罪惡，主帥屢責之。

translations.literal: His attendant Zhang Bochao enjoyed favor and committed many crimes; the commandant repeatedly reproved him.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite Zhang Bochao committed many crimes; the commandant repeatedly reproved him.

sentences.zh: 伯超懼，說休茂曰：「主帥密疏官過失，欲以啟聞，如此恐無好。」。

translations.literal: Bochao was afraid and said to Xiumao, "The commandant has secretly memorialized the officials' faults and wishes to report them — in such a case I fear there will be no good outcome."
translations.idiomatic: Bochao grew afraid and said to Xiumao, "The commandant has secretly memorialized our faults to the throne — if this reaches the court, we are finished."

sentences.zh: 休茂曰：「為之奈何？」

translations.literal: Xiumao said, "What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiumao said, "What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 伯超曰：「唯有殺行事及主帥，舉兵自衛。

translations.literal: Bochao said, "There is only killing the acting prefect and the commandant and raising troops to defend ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Bochao said, "We must kill the acting prefect and the commandant and raise troops in our own defense.

sentences.zh: 此去都數千里，縱大事不成，不失入虜中為王。」

translations.literal: From here to the capital is several thousand li; even if the great affair does not succeed, we will not fail to enter the barbarians' lands and become kings."
translations.idiomatic: The capital is thousands of li away; even if we fail, we can flee into barbarian lands and make ourselves kings."

sentences.zh: 休茂從之。

translations.literal: Xiumao followed this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiumao agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙午夜，休茂與伯超等帥夾轂隊，殺典簽楊慶於城中，出金城，殺深之及典簽戴雙；

translations.literal: At midnight on bingwu, Xiumao with Bochao and others led the flank-guard companies, killed Chief Clerk Yang Qing in the city, went out through the Golden Gate, and killed Shenzhi and Chief Clerk Dai Shuang;
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on bingwu, Xiumao with Bochao and others led the flank-guard companies, killed Chief Clerk Yang Qing in the city, went out through the Golden Gate, and killed Shenzhi and Chief Clerk Dai Shuang;

sentences.zh: 徵集兵眾，建牙馳檄，使佐吏上己為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加黃鉞。

translations.literal: gathered troops, raised the command standard and sent out proclamations, and had his aides memorialize that he was General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the yellow battle-axe added.
translations.idiomatic: mustered troops, raised the command standard and sent out proclamations, and had his aides memorialize his appointment as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the yellow battle-axe added.

sentences.zh: 侍讀博士荀詵諫，休茂殺之。

translations.literal: Lecturer-Reader Doctor Xun Shen remonstrated; Xiumao killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturer-Reader Doctor Xun Shen remonstrated; Xiumao had him killed.

sentences.zh: 伯超專任軍政，生殺在己，休茂左右曹萬期挺身斫休茂，不克而死。

translations.literal: Bochao monopolized military and civil affairs; life and death were in his hands; Xiumao's attendant Cao Wanqi threw himself forward to strike Xiumao, failed, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bochao monopolized military and civil affairs with power of life and death; Xiumao's attendant Cao Wanqi threw himself forward to strike Xiumao down, failed, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 休茂出城行營，咨議參軍沈暢之等帥眾閉門拒之。

translations.literal: Xiumao went out of the city to inspect the camp; Advisory Staff Officer Shen Changzhi and others led troops to shut the gate and bar him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiumao went out to inspect the camp, Advisory Staff Officer Shen Changzhi and others led troops to shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 休茂馳還，不得入。

translations.literal: Xiumao galloped back but could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiumao galloped back but could not enter.

sentences.zh: 義成太守薛繼考為休茂盡力攻城，克之，斬暢之及同謀數十人。

translations.literal: Yicheng Administrator Xue Jikao exerted himself to the utmost in assaulting the city for Xiumao, took it, and beheaded Changzhi and several dozen co-conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng Administrator Xue Jikao threw all his strength into assaulting the city for Xiumao, took it, and beheaded Changzhi and several dozen co-conspirators.

sentences.zh: 其日，參軍尹玄慶復起兵攻休茂，生擒，斬之，母、妻皆自殺，同黨伏誅。

translations.literal: That same day, Staff Officer Yin Xuanqing again raised troops to attack Xiumao, captured him alive and beheaded him; his mother and wife both killed themselves, and his accomplices were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, Staff Officer Yin Xuanqing raised troops again, captured Xiumao alive and beheaded him; his mother and wife killed themselves, and his accomplices were executed.

sentences.zh: 城中擾亂，莫相統攝。

translations.literal: Within the city there was turmoil, and no one directed the others.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell into turmoil with no one in command.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍劉恭之，秀之之弟也，眾共推行府州事。

translations.literal: Central Troops Staff Officer Liu Gongzhi, Xiuzhi's younger brother, was jointly advanced by the multitude to conduct the prefectural and commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Central Troops Staff Officer Liu Gongzhi, Liu Xiuzhi's younger brother, was chosen by common consent to conduct the prefectural and commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 繼考以兵脅恭之，使作啟事，言「繼考立義」，自乘驛還都；

translations.literal: Jikao used troops to coerce Gongzhi into drafting a memorial saying "Jikao established righteousness," and himself took the post relay back to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Jikao used troops to coerce Gongzhi into drafting a memorial claiming he had "upheld righteousness," then took the post relay back to the capital himself;

sentences.zh: 上以為北中郎咨議參軍，賜爵冠軍侯；

translations.literal: the emperor made him Advisory Staff Officer of the North Central Commandant and granted the title Marquis of Champion;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor appointed him Advisory Staff Officer of the North Central Commandant and granted him the title Marquis of Champion;

sentences.zh: 事尋洩，伏誅。

translations.literal: the affair was soon exposed, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: the affair was soon exposed, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 以玄慶為射聲校尉。

translations.literal: Xuanqing was made Chief of the She Sheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanqing was appointed Chief of the She Sheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 上自即位以來，抑黜諸弟；

translations.literal: Since the emperor had taken the throne, he had suppressed and demoted his younger brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne, the emperor had suppressed and demoted his younger brothers;

sentences.zh: 既克廣陵，欲更峻其科。

translations.literal: having taken Guangling, he wished to make their penalties still harsher.
translations.idiomatic: having taken Guangling, he wished to make their penalties still harsher.

sentences.zh: 沈懷文曰：「漢明不使其子比光武之子，前史以為美談。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiwen said, "Emperor Ming of Han did not let his sons compare with Emperor Guangwu's sons — former histories regarded this as fine praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen said, "Emperor Ming of Han did not let his sons compare with Emperor Guangwu's sons — the histories praise this as exemplary.

sentences.zh: 陛下既明管、蔡之誅，願崇唐、衛之寄。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, having made clear the punishments of Guan and Cai, should wish to exalt the entrustments of Tang and Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, having punished rebellion as the Duke of Zhou punished Guan and Cai, should show the forbearance the Duke of Zhou showed Tang and Wei."

sentences.zh: 及襄陽平，太宰義恭探知上旨，復上表請裁抑諸王，不使任邊州，及悉輸器甲，禁絕賓客；

translations.literal: When Xiangyang was pacified, Grand Tutor Yigong, probing the emperor's intent, again submitted a memorial requesting restraint on the princes — not allowing them to hold border provinces, requiring them all to turn in weapons and armor, and cutting off their guests;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang was pacified, Grand Tutor Liu Yigong, sensing the emperor's intent, again memorialized requesting tighter restrictions on the princes — barring them from border provinces, requiring them to surrender all weapons and armor, and cutting off their guests;

sentences.zh: 沈懷文固諫，以為不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiwen firmly remonstrated, holding this impossible, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen firmly remonstrated that this was wrong, and the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 上畋游無度，嘗出，夜還，敕開門。

translations.literal: The emperor hunted and roamed without limit; once he went out and returned at night, ordering the gate opened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hunted without restraint; once he went out and returned at night, ordering the gate opened.

sentences.zh: 侍中謝莊居守，以棨信或虛，執不奉旨，須墨敕乃開。

translations.literal: Attendant Within Xie Zhuang was on guard; holding that the tallies might be false, he refused to obey the order and required an ink edict before opening.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Within Xie Zhuang was on guard; suspecting the tallies might be forged, he refused to obey until he received an ink edict.

sentences.zh: 上後因燕飲，從容曰：「卿欲效郅君章邪？」

translations.literal: Later, at a banquet, the emperor said at ease, "Do you wish to imitate Zhi Junzhang?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a banquet, the emperor said lightly, "Do you wish to imitate Zhi Junzhang?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞王者祭祀、畋游，出入有節。

translations.literal: He answered, "I have heard that a king's sacrifices and hunting, his comings and goings, all have their proper limits.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have heard that a king's sacrifices and hunting, his comings and goings, all have their proper limits.

sentences.zh: 今陛下晨往宵歸，臣恐不逞之徒，妄生矯詐。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty goes out in the morning and returns at night — I fear that unscrupulous men may rashly produce forged deceits.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty goes out in the morning and returns at night — I fear unscrupulous men may forge orders in your name.

sentences.zh: 是以伏須神筆，乃敢開門耳。」

translations.literal: Therefore I bow and wait for the divine brush before I dare open the gate."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I waited for Your Majesty's own written order before I dared open the gate."

sentences.zh: 魏大旱，詔：「州郡境內，神無大小，悉灑掃致禱；

translations.literal: Wei suffered great drought; an edict said, "Within the borders of provinces and commanderies, spirits great and small — all are to be swept clean and prayed to;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei suffered a great drought; an edict ordered, "Within every province and commandery, spirits great and small are to be swept clean and prayed to;

sentences.zh: 俟豐登，各以其秩祭之。」

translations.literal: when the harvest is abundant, each is to be sacrificed to according to its rank."
translations.idiomatic: when the harvest is abundant, each is to receive sacrifice according to its rank."

sentences.zh: 於是群祀之廢者皆復其舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon all communal sacrifices that had been abolished were restored to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all communal sacrifices that had been abolished were restored.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊寅，魏主立其弟小新成為濟陽王，加征東大將軍，鎮平原；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, the Wei ruler enfeoffed his younger brother Xiaoxincheng as Prince of Jiyang, added Campaign-east Grand General, and stationed him at Pingyuan;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on wuyin, the Northern Wei emperor enfeoffed his younger brother Xiaoxincheng as Prince of Jiyang, appointed him Campaign-east Grand General, and stationed him at Pingyuan;

sentences.zh: 天賜為汝陰王，加征南大將軍，鎮虎牢；

translations.literal: Tianci as Prince of Ruyin, added Campaign-south Grand General, stationed at Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: Tianci as Prince of Ruyin, appointed Campaign-south Grand General, stationed at Hulao;

sentences.zh: 萬壽為樂浪王，加征北大將軍，鎮和龍；

translations.literal: Wanshou as Prince of Lelang, added Campaign-north Grand General, stationed at Helong;
translations.idiomatic: Wanshou as Prince of Lelang, appointed Campaign-north Grand General, stationed at Helong;

sentences.zh: 洛侯為廣平王。

translations.literal: Luohou as Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou as Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 壬午，魏主巡山北；

translations.literal: On renwu, the Wei ruler toured north of the mountains;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the Northern Wei emperor toured north of the mountains;

sentences.zh: 八月，丁丑，還平城。

translations.literal: in the eighth month, on dingchou, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month, on dingchou, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 戊子，立皇子子仁為永嘉王，子真為始安王。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the princes Ziren was made Prince of Yongjia and Zizhen Prince of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Prince Ziren was made Prince of Yongjia and Zizhen Prince of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the jiayin new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the jiayin new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之固讓司空，柳元景固讓開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi firmly declined the post of Minister of Works; Liu Yuanjing firmly declined Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi firmly declined the post of Minister of Works; Liu Yuanjing firmly declined Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon;

sentences.zh: 詔許之，仍命慶之朝會位次司空，俸祿依三司，元景在從公之上。

translations.literal: an edict permitted this, but still ordered Qingzhi's court assembly rank to follow the Minister of Works, his salary to follow the Three Excellencies, and Yuanjing to stand above the secondary excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: an edict permitted this, but still ranked Qingzhi at court assembly as Minister of Works with Three Excellencies salary, and placed Yuanjing above the secondary excellencies.

sentences.zh: 慶之目不知書，家素富，產業累萬金，童奴千計；

translations.literal: Qingzhi could not read by eye; his family had long been wealthy, with estates worth tens of thousands in gold and child servants numbering in the thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was illiterate; his family had long been wealthy, with estates worth tens of thousands in gold and more than a thousand servants;

sentences.zh: 再獻錢千萬，谷萬斛。

translations.literal: he twice presented ten million in cash and ten thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: he twice presented ten million in cash and ten thousand hu of grain to the court.

sentences.zh: 先有四宅，又有園捨在婁湖；

translations.literal: He previously had four mansions, and also had gardens and lodges at Lou Lake;
translations.idiomatic: He owned four mansions and also had gardens and lodges at Lou Lake;

sentences.zh: 慶之一夕攜子孫及中表親戚徙居婁湖，以四宅輸官。

translations.literal: in one night Qingzhi moved with his sons, grandsons, and cousins by marriage to Lou Lake and presented the four mansions to the government.
translations.idiomatic: in one night he moved with his sons, grandsons, and cousins to Lou Lake and presented the four mansions to the government.

sentences.zh: 慶之多蓄妓妾，優遊無事，盡意歡娛，非朝賀不出門；

translations.literal: Qingzhi kept many singing girls and concubines, wandered at ease with nothing to do, and gave himself wholly to pleasure; except for court congratulations he did not go out;
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi kept many singing girls and concubines, lived at ease with nothing to do, and gave himself wholly to pleasure; except for court audiences he never went out;

sentences.zh: 車馬率素，從者不過三五人，遇之者不知其三公也。

translations.literal: his carriage and horses were uniformly plain, his followers no more than three or five men — those who met him did not know he was one of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: his carriage and horses were plain, his followers no more than three or five — those who met him on the road did not know he was one of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，移南豫州治於湖。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the seat of Southern Yuzhou was moved to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the seat of Southern Yuzhou was moved to Yu.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以潯陽王子房為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Prince Zifang of Xunyang was made Governor of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Prince Zifang of Xunyang was appointed Governor of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊子，皇太子妃何氏卒，謚曰獻妃。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on wuzi, the crown prince's consort Lady He died; her posthumous title was Consort Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wuzi, Crown Prince's Consort Lady He died; her posthumous title was Consort Xian.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，更以歷陽王子頊為臨海王。

translations.literal: On renyin, Prince Zixu of Liyang was again made Prince of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Prince Zixu of Liyang was transferred to be Prince of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲寅，以南徐州刺史劉延孫為尚書左僕射，右僕射劉秀之為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiayin, Southern Xuzhou Governor Liu Yansun was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Right Vice Director Liu Xiuzhi was made Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on jiayin, Southern Xuzhou Governor Liu Yansun was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Right Vice Director Liu Xiuzhi was appointed Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以新安王子鸞為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On yimao, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an was made Governor of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an was appointed Governor of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子鸞母殷淑儀，寵傾後宮，子鸞愛冠諸子，凡為上所眄遇者，莫不入子鸞之府。

translations.literal: Ziluan's mother was Lady Yin the Cultivated Consort, whose favor overwhelmed the rear palace; Ziluan's love surpassed all the princes — whoever received the emperor's glance was admitted into Ziluan's household.
translations.idiomatic: Ziluan's mother was Lady Yin the Cultivated Consort, whose favor overwhelmed the inner palace; Ziluan was the emperor's favorite son — everyone the emperor favored was admitted into Ziluan's household.

sentences.zh: 及為南徐州，割吳郡以屬之。

translations.literal: When he became Governor of Southern Xuzhou, Wu commandery was carved off and made subject to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Governor of Southern Xuzhou, Wu commandery was carved off and attached to his domain.

sentences.zh: 初，巴陵王休若為北徐州刺史，以山陰令張岱為咨議參軍，行府、州、國事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Xiuruo of Baling was Governor of Northern Xuzhou and made Shanyin Magistrate Zhang Dai Advisory Staff Officer, acting in the prefectural, commandery, and princely state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Xiuruo of Baling, as Governor of Northern Xuzhou, appointed Shanyin Magistrate Zhang Dai Advisory Staff Officer to conduct the prefectural, commandery, and princely state affairs.

sentences.zh: 後臨海王子頊為廣州，豫章王子尚為揚州，晉安王子勳為南兗州，岱歷為三府咨議、三王行事，與典簽、主帥共事，事舉而情不相失。

translations.literal: Later Prince Zixu of Linhai was at Guangzhou, Prince Zishang of Yuzhang at Yangzhou, and Prince Zixun of Jin'an at Southern Yanzhou — Dai successively served as advisory staff officer of three households and acting prefect for three princes, working together with chief clerks and commandants; affairs were concluded without loss of mutual regard.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Zixu of Linhai held Guangzhou, Prince Zishang of Yuzhang held Yangzhou, and Prince Zixun of Jin'an held Southern Yanzhou — Dai served successively as advisory officer and acting prefect for all three, working alongside chief clerks and commandants; affairs were concluded without loss of mutual regard.

sentences.zh: 或謂岱曰：「主王既幼，執事多門，而每能緝和公私，雲何致此？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Dai, "The ruling prince is young and those in charge are many — yet you can each time harmonize public and private affairs; how do you achieve this?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Dai, "The princes are young and many hands hold power — yet you harmonize public and private affairs every time; how do you manage it?"

sentences.zh: 岱曰：「古人言：『一心可以事百君。』

translations.literal: Dai said, "The ancients said, 'With one heart one may serve a hundred lords.'
translations.idiomatic: Dai said, "The ancients said, 'With one heart one may serve a hundred lords.'

sentences.zh: 我為政端平，待物以禮，悔吝之事，無由而及；

translations.literal: I govern with upright fairness and treat things with ritual propriety — matters of regret have no way to reach me;
