translations.idiomatic: I govern with upright fairness and treat everyone with ritual propriety — matters of regret never touch me;

sentences.zh: 明暗短長，更是才用之多少耳。」

translations.literal: brightness and darkness, strength and weakness — these are rather a matter of how much talent is applied."
translations.idiomatic: success and failure are merely a matter of how much talent one brings to bear."

sentences.zh: 及子鸞為南徐州，復以岱為別駕、行事。

translations.literal: When Ziluan became Governor of Southern Xuzhou, Dai was again made Vice Director and acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziluan became Governor of Southern Xuzhou, Dai was again appointed Vice Director and acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 岱，永之弟也。

translations.literal: Dai was Yongzhi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Dai was Zhang Yongzhi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 魏員外散騎常侍游明根等來聘。

translations.literal: You Minggen, Attendant Cavalier Extraordinary of Wei, and others came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: You Minggen, Attendant Cavalier Extraordinary of Northern Wei, and others came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 明根，雅之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Minggen was a younger cousin of Yazhi on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen was a younger cousin of Yazhi on the paternal side.

sentences.zh: 魏廣平王洛侯卒。

translations.literal: Prince Luohou of Guangping of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Luohou of Guangping under Northern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，以領軍將軍劉遵考為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renshen, Director of the Palace Guards Liu Zunkao was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen, Director of the Palace Guards Liu Zunkao was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，制民戶歲輸布四匹。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, it was decreed that each household was to deliver four bolts of cloth annually.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, it was decreed that each household was to deliver four bolts of cloth annually.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔士族雜婚者皆補將吏。

translations.literal: This year, an edict ordered that gentry families in mixed marriages were all to be assigned as generals and officers.
translations.idiomatic: This year, an edict ordered that gentry families in mixed marriages were all to be conscripted as generals and officers.

sentences.zh: 士族多避役逃亡，乃嚴為之制，捕得即斬之，往往奔竄湖山為盜賊。

translations.literal: Many gentry families evaded corvée and fled; strict regulations were then imposed — whoever was captured was immediately beheaded, and many often fled into lakes and mountains to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Many gentry families evaded corvée and fled; strict regulations were imposed — anyone captured was immediately beheaded, and many fled into lakes and mountains to become bandits.

sentences.zh: 沈懷文諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiwen remonstrated; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen remonstrated; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝下大明六年（

translations.literal: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu, Continued — sixth year of Daming (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Continued — Sixth Year of Daming (

sentences.zh: 壬寅，公元四六二年）

translations.literal: renyin, corresponding to the year 462 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: renyin, corresponding to 462 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸未，魏樂浪王萬壽卒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, Prince Wanshou of Lelang of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on guiwei, Prince Wanshou of Lelang under Northern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上初祀五帝於明堂，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the emperor for the first time sacrificed to the Five Emperors at the Bright Hall and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the emperor for the first time sacrificed to the Five Emperors at the Bright Hall and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丁未，策秀、孝於中堂。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the examination of the cultivated and filial was held in the central hall.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the examination of the cultivated and filial was held in the central hall.

sentences.zh: 揚州秀才顧法對策曰：「源清則流潔，神聖則刑全。

translations.literal: Yangzhou cultivated talent Gu Fa answered in the examination, saying, "When the source is clear, the stream is pure; when the spirit is sacred, punishments are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou cultivated talent Gu Fa answered in the examination: "When the source is clear, the stream runs pure; when the sovereign is sacred, punishments are complete.

sentences.zh: 躬化易於上風，體訓速於草偃。」

translations.literal: Personal transformation is easier than wind from above; embodying instruction is swifter than grass bending down."
translations.idiomatic: Personal transformation spreads easier than wind from above; embodied instruction works swifter than grass bending in the breeze."

sentences.zh: 上覽之，惡其諒也，投策於地。

translations.literal: The emperor, reading it, hated its bluntness and threw the examination slip to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, reading it, hated its bluntness and threw the examination slip to the ground.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯，復百官祿。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yimao, official salaries were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yimao, official salaries were restored.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚寅，立皇子子元為邵陵王。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengyin, Prince Ziyuan was made Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengyin, Prince Ziyuan was made Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 初，侍中沈懷文，數以直諫忤旨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Attendant Within Shen Huaiwen had several times through blunt remonstrance offended the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Attendant Within Shen Huaiwen had several times offended the emperor through blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 懷文素與顏竣、周朗善，上謂懷文曰：「竣若知我殺之，亦當不敢如此。」

translations.literal: Huaiwen had long been on good terms with Yan Jun and Zhou Lang; the emperor said to Huaiwen, "If Jun had known I would kill him, he also would not have dared to act thus."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen had long been close to Yan Jun and Zhou Lang; the emperor said to him, "If Jun had known I would kill him, he would not have dared act as he did."

sentences.zh: 懷文嘿然。

translations.literal: Huaiwen was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen was silent.

sentences.zh: 侍中王彧，言次稱竣、朗人才之美，懷文與相酬和。

translations.literal: Attendant Within Wang Yu, in the course of conversation, praised the excellence of Jun and Lang's talents; Huaiwen responded in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Within Wang Yu praised Jun and Lang's talents in conversation; Huaiwen joined in agreement.

sentences.zh: 顏師伯以白上，上益不悅。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo reported this to the emperor, and the emperor grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo reported this to the emperor, who grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 上嘗出射雉，風雨驟至。

translations.literal: The emperor once went out to shoot pheasants; wind and rain suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once went out pheasant hunting when wind and rain suddenly struck.

sentences.zh: 懷文與王彧、江智淵約相與諫。

translations.literal: Huaiwen with Wang Yu and Jiang Zhiyuan agreed to remonstrate together.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen agreed with Wang Yu and Jiang Zhiyuan to remonstrate together.

sentences.zh: 會召入雉場，懷文曰：「風雨如此，非聖躬所宜冒。」

translations.literal: When they were summoned into the pheasant ground, Huaiwen said, "Wind and rain such as this are not what the sacred person ought to brave."
translations.idiomatic: When they were summoned into the pheasant ground, Huaiwen said, "Wind and rain such as this are not fit for Your Majesty to brave."

sentences.zh: 彧曰：「懷文所啟，宜從。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "What Huaiwen has stated ought to be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Huaiwen is right — Your Majesty should heed him."

sentences.zh: 智淵未及言，上注弩作色曰：「卿欲效顏竣邪，何以恆知人事！」

translations.literal: Zhiyuan had not yet spoken when the emperor, fixing his crossbow and changing color, said, "Do you wish to imitate Yan Jun — why do you always know human affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhiyuan could speak, the emperor fixed his crossbow and said angrily, "Do you wish to imitate Yan Jun — why do you always know what is best!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「顏竣小子，恨不先鞭其面！」

translations.literal: He also said, "That petty fellow Yan Jun — I regret I did not first whip his face!"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "That wretch Yan Jun — I regret I did not whip his face first!"

sentences.zh: 每上燕集，在坐者皆令沉醉，嘲謔無度。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor held a banquet, those seated were all made thoroughly drunk; mockery and jesting knew no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet the emperor held, those seated were made thoroughly drunk while mockery and jesting knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 懷文素不飲酒，又不好戲調，上謂故欲異己。

translations.literal: Huaiwen by nature did not drink wine and also did not enjoy playful banter; the emperor said he deliberately wished to set himself apart.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen did not drink and disliked playful banter; the emperor said he deliberately set himself apart.

sentences.zh: 謝莊嘗戒懷文曰：「卿每與人異，亦何可久！」

translations.literal: Xie Zhuang once warned Huaiwen, "You are always different from others — how can this last long!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhuang once warned him, "You are always different from everyone else — how long can that last!"

sentences.zh: 懷文曰：「吾少來如此，豈可一朝而變！

translations.literal: Huaiwen said, "I have been thus from youth — how can I change in a single morning!
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said, "I have been this way since youth — how can I change overnight!

sentences.zh: 非欲異物，性所得耳。」

translations.literal: It is not that I wish to set myself apart — it is what my nature has obtained."
translations.idiomatic: I do not mean to set myself apart — it is simply my nature."

sentences.zh: 上乃出懷文為晉安王子勳征虜長史，領廣陵太守。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Huaiwen out as Campaign-against-Barbarians Chief of Staff to Prince Zixun of Jin'an, concurrently holding the post of Guangling Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Huaiwen out as Campaign-against-Barbarians Chief of Staff to Prince Zixun of Jin'an, with concurrent appointment as Guangling Administrator.

sentences.zh: 懷文詣建康朝正，事畢遣還，以女病求申期，至是猶未發，為有司所糾，免官，禁錮十年。

translations.literal: Huaiwen went to Jiankang for the New Year audience; when the business was concluded he was sent back, but requested extension on account of his daughter's illness — by this time he had still not departed and was impeached by the relevant offices, dismissed from office, and confined for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen went to Jiankang for the New Year audience; when the business was concluded he was sent back, but requested extension on account of his daughter's illness — by then he had still not departed and was impeached, dismissed from office, and confined for ten years.

sentences.zh: 懷文賣宅，欲還東，上聞之，大怒，收付廷尉，丁未，賜懷文死。

translations.literal: Huaiwen sold his house, wishing to return east; the emperor heard of this, was greatly enraged, took him into custody and handed him to the Court of Justice; on dingwei, Huaiwen was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen sold his house, wishing to return east; the emperor heard of this, flew into a rage, arrested him and handed him to the Court of Justice; on dingwei, Huaiwen was granted death.

sentences.zh: 懷文三子澹、淵、沖，行哭為懷文請命，見者傷之。

translations.literal: Huaiwen's three sons Dan, Yuan, and Chong went weeping to beg for his life; those who saw it were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen's three sons Dan, Yuan, and Chong went weeping to beg for his life; all who saw them were moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 柳元景欲救懷文，言於上曰：「沈懷文三子，塗炭不可見；

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing wished to save Huaiwen and said to the emperor, "Shen Huaiwen's three sons are in such torment they cannot be looked upon;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing wished to save Huaiwen and said to the emperor, "Shen Huaiwen's three sons are in such torment they cannot be looked upon;

sentences.zh: 願陛下速正其罪。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty quickly to settle his crime."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to settle his case quickly."

sentences.zh: 上竟殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor killed him anyway.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，淑儀殷氏卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Cultivated Consort Lady Yin died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Cultivated Consort Lady Yin died.

sentences.zh: 追拜貴妃，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: She was posthumously made Noble Consort; her posthumous title was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made Noble Consort with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 上痛悼不已，精神為之惘惘，頗廢政事。

translations.literal: The emperor's grief and mourning did not cease; his spirit was dazed thereby, and he largely neglected state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's grief would not cease; his spirit grew dazed, and he largely neglected state affairs.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬寅，太宰義恭解領司徒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renyin, Grand Tutor Yigong relinquished his concurrent post as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renyin, Grand Tutor Liu Yigong relinquished his concurrent post as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛酉，東昌文穆公劉延孫卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinyou, Duke Wenmu of Dongchang Liu Yansun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinyou, Duke Wenmu of Dongchang Liu Yansun died.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Wei ruler went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Northern Wei emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 魏石樓胡賀略孫反，長安鎮將陸真討平之。

translations.literal: The Shilou Hu Heluesun of Wei rebelled; Chang'an Garrison General Lu Zhen suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shilou Hu Heluesun under Northern Wei rebelled; Chang'an Garrison General Lu Zhen suppressed and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 魏主命真城長蛇鎮。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered Zhen to fortify Changshe Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor ordered Zhen to fortify Changshe Fort.

sentences.zh: 氐豪仇辱檀反，真討平之，卒城而還。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Qiurutan rebelled; Zhen suppressed and pacified him, completed the fort, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Qiurutan rebelled; Zhen suppressed him, completed the fort, and returned.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬寅，魏主如河西。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, the Wei ruler went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on renyin, the Northern Wei emperor went to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 乙未，立皇子子雲為晉陵王；

translations.literal: On yiwei, Prince Ziyun was made Prince of Jinling;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Prince Ziyun was made Prince of Jinling;

sentences.zh: 是日卒，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: that same day he died; his posthumous title was Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: that same day he died; his posthumous title was Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 初，晉庾冰議使沙門敬王者，桓玄複述其議，並不果行。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Bing of Jin had proposed that Buddhist monks bow to the ruler; Huan Xuan repeated the proposal — neither was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yu Bing of Jin had proposed that Buddhist monks bow to the ruler; Huan Xuan repeated the proposal — neither was carried out.

sentences.zh: 至是，上使有司奏曰：「儒、法枝派，名、墨條分，至於崇親嚴上，厥猷靡爽。

translations.literal: At this time, the emperor had the relevant offices memorialize, saying, "Confucianism and Legalism branch into schools, Names and Mohism divide into lines — yet in honoring kin and revering superiors, their principles do not err.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, the emperor had the relevant offices memorialize: "Confucianism and Legalism branch into schools, Names and Mohism divide into lines — yet in honoring kin and revering superiors, their principles do not err.

sentences.zh: 唯浮圖為教，反經提傳，拘文蔽道，在末爾扇。

translations.literal: Only the Buddha's teaching as a doctrine turns against the classics and lifts up heterodox transmission, binding by texts and obscuring the Way — at the end it fans such things.
translations.idiomatic: Only Buddhism as a doctrine turns against the classics and lifts up heterodox transmission, binding by texts and obscuring the Way — at the end it fans such things.

sentences.zh: 夫佛以謙卑自牧，忠虔為道，寧有屈膝四輩而簡禮二親，稽顙耆臘而直體萬乘者哉！

translations.literal: The Buddha takes humility and self-restraint, loyalty and devotion as the Way — how could there be bending the knee to the four ranks while simplifying ritual toward the two parents, or knocking the forehead to aged monks while standing erect before the ten-thousand-chariot ruler!
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha teaches humility and devotion — how could monks bend the knee to the four ranks while simplifying ritual toward their parents, or prostrate before aged monks while standing erect before the emperor!

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，以為沙門接見，比當盡虔；

translations.literal: We your ministers jointly deliberate and hold that when monks are received in audience, they should be fully reverent;
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers jointly hold that when monks are received in audience, they should be fully reverent;

sentences.zh: 禮敬之容，依其本俗。」

translations.literal: the bearing of ritual respect should follow their original custom."
translations.idiomatic: the bearing of ritual respect should follow their original custom."

sentences.zh: 九月，戊寅，制沙門致敬人主。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuyin, it was decreed that monks were to bow to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuyin, it was decreed that monks were to bow to the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 及廢帝即位，復舊。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, the former practice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, the former practice was restored.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以尚書右僕射劉遵考為左僕射，丹陽尹王僧朗為右僕射。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Zunkao was made Left Vice Director, and Danyang Prefect Wang Senglang was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Right Vice Director Liu Zunkao was appointed Left Vice Director, and Danyang Prefect Wang Senglang was appointed Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 僧朗，彧之父也。

translations.literal: Senglang was Yu's father.
translations.idiomatic: Senglang was Wang Yu's father.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬申，葬宣貴妃於龍山。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renshen, Noble Consort Xuan was buried at Long Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on renshen, Noble Consort Xuan was buried at Long Mountain.

sentences.zh: 鑿岡通道數十里，民不堪役，死亡甚眾；

translations.literal: Hills were cut through and passages opened for several tens of li; the people could not bear the corvée, and deaths were very numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Hills were cut through and passages opened for tens of li; the people could not bear the corvée, and deaths were very numerous;

sentences.zh: 自江南葬埋之盛，未之有也。

translations.literal: since the Jin crossed the Yangzi, there had never been such magnificence in burial.
translations.idiomatic: since the Jin crossed the Yangzi, there had never been such magnificence in burial.

sentences.zh: 又為之別立廟。

translations.literal: A separate temple was also built for her.
translations.idiomatic: A separate temple was also built for her.

sentences.zh: 魏員外散騎常侍游明根等來聘。

translations.literal: You Minggen, Attendant Cavalier Extraordinary of Wei, and others came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: You Minggen, Attendant Cavalier Extraordinary of Northern Wei, and others came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，加尚書令柳元景司空。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Director of the Secretariat Liu Yuanjing was given the additional title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Director of the Secretariat Liu Yuanjing was given the additional title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 南徐州從事史范陽祖沖之上言，何承天《元嘉歷》疏舛猶多，更造新歷，以為：「舊法，冬至日有定處，未盈百載，輒差二度；

translations.literal: Southern Xuzhou Attendant Clerk Zu Chongzhi of Fanyang submitted a memorial saying that He Chengtian's Yuanjia Calendar still had many errors and gaps, and proposed a new calendar, holding: "Under the old method, the winter solstice had a fixed position; before a full hundred years had passed, it would already differ by two degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Xuzhou Attendant Clerk Zu Chongzhi of Fanyang memorialized that He Chengtian's Yuanjia Calendar still had many errors, and proposed a new calendar: "Under the old method, the winter solstice had a fixed position; before a full century had passed, it would already differ by two degrees;

sentences.zh: 今令冬至日度，歲歲微差，將來久用，無煩屢改。

translations.literal: now let the winter solstice's degree shift slightly year by year — in long future use there will be no need for repeated revisions.
translations.idiomatic: now let the winter solstice's degree shift slightly year by year — in long use there will be no need for repeated revisions.

sentences.zh: 又，子為辰首，位在正北，虛為北方列宿之中；

translations.literal: Further, zi is the head of the earthly branches, positioned due north; xu is among the northern constellations;
translations.idiomatic: Further, zi is the head of the earthly branches, positioned due north; xu is among the northern constellations;

sentences.zh: 今歷，上元日度，發自虛一。

translations.literal: in the present calendar, the superior origin's solar degree begins from xu one.
translations.idiomatic: in the present calendar, the superior origin's solar degree begins from xu one.

sentences.zh: 又，日辰之號，甲子為先；

translations.literal: Further, among the designations of days and branches, jiazi comes first;
translations.idiomatic: Further, among the designations of days and branches, jiazi comes first;

sentences.zh: 今歷，上元歲在甲子。

translations.literal: in the present calendar, the superior origin year is in jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: in the present calendar, the superior origin year is in jiazi.

sentences.zh: 又，承天法，日、月、五星各自有元；

translations.literal: Further, in Chengtian's method, sun, moon, and the five planets each had their own origin;
translations.idiomatic: Further, in Chengtian's method, sun, moon, and the five planets each had their own origin;

sentences.zh: 今法，交會、遲疾悉以上元歲首為始。」

translations.literal: in the present method, conjunctions and fast-slow motions all begin from the superior origin year's head."
translations.idiomatic: in the present method, conjunctions and fast-slow motions all begin from the superior origin year's head."

sentences.zh: 上令善歷者難之，不能屈。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered those skilled in calendars to challenge him; they could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered calendar experts to challenge him; they could not refute him.

sentences.zh: 會上晏駕，不果施行。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor died suddenly, and it was not put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the emperor died suddenly, and it was not put into practice.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝下大明七年（

translations.literal: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu, Continued — seventh year of Daming (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Continued — Seventh Year of Daming (

sentences.zh: 癸卯，公元四六三年）

translations.literal: guimao, corresponding to the year 463 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: guimao, corresponding to 463 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁亥，以尚書右僕射王僧朗為太常，衛將軍顏師伯為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dinghai, Right Vice Director Wang Senglang was made Minister of Ceremonies, and Guard General Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dinghai, Right Vice Director Wang Senglang was appointed Minister of Ceremonies, and Guard General Yan Shibo was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上每因宴集，好使群臣自相嘲訐以為樂。

translations.literal: At every banquet the emperor liked to have the ministers mock and accuse one another for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet the emperor liked to have his ministers mock and accuse one another for amusement.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎江智淵素恬雅，漸不會旨。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Jiang Zhiyuan was by nature quiet and refined and gradually failed to suit the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Jiang Zhiyuan was by nature quiet and refined and gradually failed to suit the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 嘗使智淵以王僧郎戲其子彧。

translations.literal: Once he had Zhiyuan use Wang Senglang to jest at his son Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had Zhiyuan use Wang Senglang to jest at his son Yu.

sentences.zh: 智淵正色曰：「恐不宜有此戲！」

translations.literal: Zhiyuan said with a stern countenance, "I fear such jesting is not fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan said gravely, "I fear such jesting is not fitting!"

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「江僧安癡人，癡人自相惜。」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily, "Jiang Seng'an is a fool — fools cherish one another."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "Jiang Seng'an is a fool — fools cherish one another."

sentences.zh: 僧安，智淵之父也。

translations.literal: Seng'an was Zhiyuan's father.
translations.idiomatic: Seng'an was Zhiyuan's father.

sentences.zh: 智淵伏席流涕，由此恩寵大衰。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan prostrated himself on the mat and wept; from this his favor greatly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan prostrated himself on the mat and wept; from this his favor greatly declined.

sentences.zh: 又議殷遺妃謚曰懷，上以為不盡美，甚銜之。

translations.literal: When the posthumous title Huai was proposed for the late Lady Yin, the emperor held it did not fully express her excellence and deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: When the posthumous title Huai was proposed for the late Lady Yin, the emperor held it did not fully express her excellence and deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 它日，與群臣乘馬至貴妃墓，舉鞭指墓前石柱，謂智淵曰：「此上不容有『懷』字！」

translations.literal: Another day, riding with the ministers to the Noble Consort's tomb, he raised his whip and pointed at the stone pillar before the tomb, saying to Zhiyuan, "On this there cannot be the character 'Huai'!"
translations.idiomatic: Another day, riding with the ministers to the Noble Consort's tomb, he raised his whip and pointed at the stone pillar before the tomb, saying to Zhiyuan, "On this there cannot be the character 'Huai'!"

sentences.zh: 智淵益懼，竟以憂卒。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan grew still more fearful and in the end died of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan grew still more fearful and in the end died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以尚書令柳元景為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On jichou, Director of the Secretariat Liu Yuanjing was made Rapid Cavalry General, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Director of the Secretariat Liu Yuanjing was appointed Rapid Cavalry General, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，上南巡豫、南兗二州；

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiayin, the emperor made a southern tour of Yu and Southern Yan provinces;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, the emperor made a southern tour of Yu and Southern Yan provinces;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，校獵於烏江；

translations.literal: on dingmao he conducted a hunt at Wujiang;
translations.idiomatic: on dingmao he conducted a hunt at Wujiang;

sentences.zh: 壬戌，大赦；

translations.literal: on renxu a general amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: on renxu a general amnesty was proclaimed;

sentences.zh: 甲子，如瓜步山；

translations.literal: on jiazi he went to Guabu Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: on jiazi he went to Guabu Mountain;

sentences.zh: 壬申，還建康。

translations.literal: on renshen he returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: on renshen he returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，詔：「自非將軍戰陳，並不得專殺；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi, an edict said, "Except in generals' battle formations, none may kill on their own authority;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on jiazi, an edict said, "Except in generals' battle formations, none may kill on their own authority;

sentences.zh: 其罪應重辟者，皆先上須報；

translations.literal: those whose crimes deserve capital punishment must all first report upward and await reply;
translations.idiomatic: those whose crimes deserve capital punishment must all first report upward and await reply;

sentences.zh: 違犯者以殺人論。」

translations.literal: violators are to be judged as murderers."
translations.idiomatic: violators are to be judged as murderers."

sentences.zh: 五月，丙子，詔曰：「自今刺史、守宰，動民興軍，皆須手詔施行；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingzi, an edict said, "From now on governors and prefectural administrators, in mobilizing the people and raising armies, must all act on the emperor's own written order;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingzi, an edict said, "From now on governors and prefectural administrators, in mobilizing the people and raising armies, must all act on the emperor's own written order;

sentences.zh: 唯邊隅外警及奸釁內發，變起倉猝者，不從此例。」

translations.literal: only border alarms from without and treasonous outbreaks within, where change arises in sudden haste, are not subject to this rule."
translations.idiomatic: only border alarms from without and treasonous outbreaks within, where change arises suddenly, are exempt from this rule."

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以左民尚書蔡興宗、左衛將軍袁粲為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Minister of the Left People Cai Xingzong and Left Guard General Yuan Can were made Directors of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Minister of the Left People Cai Xingzong and Left Guard General Yuan Can were appointed Directors of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 粲，淑之兄子也。

translations.literal: Can was a nephew of Shuzhi on the elder brother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Can was a nephew of Yuan Shuzhi.

sentences.zh: 上好狎侮群臣，自太宰義恭以下，不免穢辱。

translations.literal: The emperor liked to treat the ministers with familiar contempt; from Grand Tutor Yigong downward, none escaped filthy insult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor liked to treat his ministers with familiar contempt; from Grand Tutor Liu Yigong downward, none escaped filthy insult.

sentences.zh: 常呼金紫光祿大夫王玄謨為老傖，僕射劉秀之為老慳，顏師伯為齴；

translations.literal: He often called Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Wang Xuanmo "Old Barbarian," Vice Director Liu Xiuzhi "Old Miser," and Yan Shibo "Gums";
translations.idiomatic: He often called Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Wang Xuanmo "Old Barbarian," Vice Director Liu Xiuzhi "Old Miser," and Yan Shibo "Gums";

sentences.zh: 其餘短、長、肥、瘦，皆有稱目。

translations.literal: the rest — short, tall, fat, thin — all had nicknames.
translations.idiomatic: the rest — short, tall, fat, thin — all had nicknames.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎宗靈秀體肥，拜起不便，每至集會，多所賜與，欲其瞻謝傾踣，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Zong Lingxiu was corpulent; bowing and rising were inconvenient for him — at every gathering the emperor gave him many gifts, wishing that when he looked up to give thanks he would topple over, taking this as laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Zong Lingxiu was corpulent and found bowing awkward — at every gathering the emperor gave him many gifts, hoping he would topple over when he looked up to give thanks, taking this as a joke.

sentences.zh: 又寵一崑崙奴，令以杖擊群臣，尚書令柳元景以下皆不能免。

translations.literal: He also favored a Kunlun slave and ordered him to strike the ministers with a staff — from Director of the Secretariat Liu Yuanjing downward, none could escape.
translations.idiomatic: He also favored a Kunlun slave and ordered him to strike the ministers with a staff — from Director Liu Yuanjing downward, none could escape.

sentences.zh: 唯憚蔡興宗方嚴，不敢侵媟。

translations.literal: Only toward Cai Xingzong, stern and square, did he fear to encroach or insult.
translations.idiomatic: Only toward Cai Xingzong, stern and upright, did he fear to encroach or insult.

sentences.zh: 顏師伯謂儀曹郎王耽之曰：「蔡尚書常免暱戲，去人實遠。」

translations.literal: Yan Shibo said to Ceremonial Officer Wang Danzhi, "Director Cai is always spared familiar jesting — he is truly far from ordinary men."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo said to Ceremonial Officer Wang Danzhi, "Director Cai is always spared the emperor's familiar jesting — he is truly far above ordinary men."

sentences.zh: 耽之曰：「蔡豫章昔在相府，亦以方嚴不狎。

translations.literal: Danzhi said, "Director Cai of Yuzhang, when he was in the chief minister's office, was also stern and square and not familiar.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhi said, "Director Cai of Yuzhang, when he was in the chief minister's office, was also stern and upright and not familiar.

sentences.zh: 武帝宴私之日，未嘗相召。

translations.literal: On Emperor Wu's private banquet days, he was never summoned.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Wu's private banquet days, he was never summoned.

sentences.zh: 蔡尚書今日可謂能負荷矣。」

translations.literal: Director Cai today may be said to bear the load."
translations.idiomatic: Director Cai today may truly be said to bear the load."

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Wei ruler went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the Northern Wei emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊辰，以秦郡太守劉德願為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuchen, Qin commandery Administrator Liu Deyuan was made Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuchen, Qin commandery Administrator Liu Deyuan was appointed Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 德願，懷慎之子也。

translations.literal: Deyuan was Huaijin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan was Liu Huaijin's son.

sentences.zh: 上既葬殷貴妃，數與群臣至其墓，謂德願曰：「卿哭貴妃，悲者當厚賞。」

translations.literal: After the emperor had buried Noble Consort Yin, he often went with the ministers to her tomb and said to Deyuan, "If you weep for the Noble Consort and are sorrowful, you shall receive a rich reward."
translations.idiomatic: After burying Noble Consort Yin, the emperor often went with his ministers to her tomb and said to Deyuan, "Whoever weeps for the Noble Consort most sorrowfully shall receive a rich reward."

sentences.zh: 德願應聲慟哭，撫膺擗踴，涕泗交流。

translations.literal: Deyuan at once wailed in grief, beating his breast and stamping his feet, tears and mucus streaming together.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan at once wailed in grief, beating his breast and stamping his feet, tears streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 上甚悅，故用豫州刺史以賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and therefore used the post of Yuzhou Governor as his reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him with the governorship of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上又令醫術人羊志哭貴妃，志亦嗚咽極悲。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered the physician Yang Zhi to weep for the Noble Consort; Zhi also sobbed with extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered the physician Yang Zhi to weep for the Noble Consort; Zhi also sobbed with extreme grief.

sentences.zh: 他日有問志者曰：「卿那得此副急淚？」

translations.literal: Another day someone asked Zhi, "How did you produce such ready tears?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day someone asked Zhi, "How did you produce such ready tears?"

sentences.zh: 志曰：「我爾日自哭亡妾耳。」

translations.literal: Zhi said, "That day I was weeping for my own dead concubine."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "That day I was weeping for my own dead concubine."

sentences.zh: 上為人機警勇決，學問博洽，文章華敏，省讀書奏，能七行俱下，又善騎射，而奢欲無度。

translations.literal: The emperor as a man was alert and brave in decision, his learning broad and comprehensive, his writing splendid and quick; in reviewing memorials he could read seven lines at once; he was also skilled at riding and archery — yet his extravagance and desires knew no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alert and decisive, learned and accomplished, his writing splendid and quick; he could read seven lines of memorials at once and was skilled at riding and archery — yet his extravagance and desires knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏渡江以來，宮室草創，朝宴所臨，東、西二堂而已。

translations.literal: Since the Jin crossed the Yangzi, palace halls had been hastily built; for court banquets there were only the eastern and western halls.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin crossed the Yangzi, palace halls had been hastily built; for court banquets there were only the eastern and western halls.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武末，始作清暑殿。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, the Clear Summer Hall was first built.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, the Clear Summer Hall was first built.

sentences.zh: 宋興，無所增改。

translations.literal: When Song arose, nothing was added or changed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song arose, nothing was added or changed.

sentences.zh: 上始大修宮室，土木被錦繡，嬖妾幸臣，賞賜傾府藏。

translations.literal: The emperor then began large-scale repair of palace halls; earth and wood were draped in brocade and embroidery; favored concubines and trusted ministers received rewards that emptied the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then began large-scale construction of palace halls; earth and wood were draped in brocade and embroidery; favored concubines and trusted ministers received rewards that emptied the treasury.

sentences.zh: 壞高祖所居陰室，於其處起玉燭殿。

translations.literal: He destroyed the shaded chamber where the High Ancestor had dwelt and on that site raised the Jade Candle Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed the shaded chamber where Emperor Gaozu had dwelt and on that site raised the Jade Candle Hall.

sentences.zh: 與群臣觀之，床頭有土障，壁上掛葛燈籠、麻蠅拂。

translations.literal: He showed it to the ministers; at the head of the bed was an earthen screen, and on the wall hung a kudzu lamp shade and a hemp fly whisk.
translations.idiomatic: He showed it to the ministers; at the head of the bed was an earthen screen, and on the wall hung a kudzu lamp shade and a hemp fly whisk.

sentences.zh: 侍中袁顗因盛稱高祖儉素之德。

translations.literal: Attendant Within Yuan Yi thereupon lavishly praised the High Ancestor's virtue of frugality and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Within Yuan Yi thereupon lavishly praised Emperor Gaozu's virtue of frugality and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 上不答，獨曰：「田舍公得此，已為過矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply, but said only, "For a rustic fellow to have gotten this much was already excessive."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply, but said only, "For a rustic fellow to have gotten this much was already excessive."

sentences.zh: 顗，淑之兄子也。

translations.literal: Yi was a nephew of Shuzhi on the elder brother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a nephew of Yuan Shuzhi.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙丑，立皇子子孟為淮南王，子產為臨賀王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yichou, Prince Zimeng was made Prince of Huainan and Zichan Prince of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on yichou, Prince Zimeng was made Prince of Huainan and Zichan Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏主畋於河西；

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Wei ruler hunted in Hexi;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Northern Wei emperor hunted in Hexi;

sentences.zh: 九月，辛巳，還平城。

translations.literal: in the ninth month, on xinsi, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month, on xinsi, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以新安王子鸞兼司徒。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an was made concurrent Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an was appointed concurrent Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 丙申，立皇子子嗣為東平王。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Prince Zisi was made Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Prince Zisi was made Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸亥，以東海王禕為司空。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guihai, Prince Yi of Donghai was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on guihai, Prince Yi of Donghai was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 己巳，上校獵姑孰。

translations.literal: On jisi, the emperor conducted a hunt at Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the emperor conducted a hunt at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 魏員外散騎常侍游明根等來聘。

translations.literal: You Minggen, Attendant Cavalier Extraordinary of Wei, and others came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: You Minggen, Attendant Cavalier Extraordinary of Northern Wei, and others came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 明根奉使三返，上以其長者，禮之有加。

translations.literal: Minggen had served as envoy three times; the emperor, because he was an elder of virtue, treated him with added ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen had served as envoy three times; the emperor, respecting him as an elder of virtue, treated him with added ceremony.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸巳，上習水軍於梁山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guisi, the emperor drilled the naval forces at Liang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guisi, the emperor drilled the naval forces at Liang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙午，如歷陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingwu, he went to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingwu, he went to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiayin, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 己未，太宰義恭加尚書令。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Grand Tutor Yigong was given the additional post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Grand Tutor Liu Yigong was given the additional post of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，上還建康。

translations.literal: On guihai, the emperor returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the emperor returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝下大明八年（

translations.literal: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu, Continued — eighth year of Daming (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Continued — Eighth Year of Daming (

sentences.zh: 甲辰，公元四六四年）

translations.literal: jiachen, corresponding to the year 464 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: jiachen, corresponding to 464 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁亥，魏主立其弟雲為任城王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dinghai, the Wei ruler enfeoffed his younger brother Yun as Prince of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dinghai, the Northern Wei emperor enfeoffed his younger brother Yun as Prince of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以徐州刺史新安王子鸞領司徒。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Xuzhou Governor Prince Ziluan of Xin'an was made concurrent Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Xuzhou Governor Prince Ziluan of Xin'an was appointed concurrent Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 夏，閏五月，壬寅，太宰義恭領太尉。

translations.literal: In summer, the intercalary fifth month, on renyin, Grand Tutor Yigong was made concurrent Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the intercalary fifth month, on renyin, Grand Tutor Liu Yigong was appointed concurrent Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 上末年尤貪財利，刺史、二千石罷還，必限使獻奉，又以蒲戲取之，要令罄盡乃止。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor was especially greedy for wealth; when governors and two-thousand-bushel officials were dismissed and returned, he always set a limit requiring them to present tribute, and also took from them through the rushes game, insisting they be utterly drained before he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor was especially greedy for wealth; when governors and two-thousand-bushel officials were dismissed and returned, he always demanded tribute, and also took from them through gambling, insisting they be utterly drained before he stopped.

sentences.zh: 終日酣飲，少有醒時，常憑几昏睡，或外有奏事，即肅然整容，無復酒態。

translations.literal: He drank heavily all day, rarely sober; he often leaned on a armrest in drowsy sleep — yet if there was business reported from outside, he at once composed his countenance with stern dignity and showed no more drunken bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily all day, rarely sober; he often leaned on an armrest in drowsy sleep — yet if business was reported from outside, he at once composed his countenance with stern dignity and showed no more drunken bearing.

sentences.zh: 由是內外畏之，莫敢弛惰。

translations.literal: Thereby within and without all feared him, and none dared grow slack or lazy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby within and without all feared him, and none dared grow slack or lazy.

sentences.zh: 庚申，上殂於玉燭殿。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the emperor died at the Jade Candle Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the emperor died at the Jade Candle Hall.

sentences.zh: 遺詔：「太宰義恭解尚書令，加中書監；

translations.literal: His testamentary edict said, "Grand Tutor Yigong is relieved of Director of the Secretariat and given Supervisor of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: His testamentary edict said, "Grand Tutor Liu Yigong is relieved of Director of the Secretariat and given Supervisor of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 以驃騎將軍、南兗州刺史柳元景領尚書令，入居城內。

translations.literal: Rapid Cavalry General and Southern Yanzhou Governor Liu Yuanjing is to hold Director of the Secretariat and reside within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rapid Cavalry General and Southern Yanzhou Governor Liu Yuanjing is to hold Director of the Secretariat and reside within the city.

sentences.zh: 事無鉅細，悉關二公，大事與始興公沈慶之參決；

translations.literal: Matters great and small are all to concern the two dukes; great affairs are to be decided with Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Matters great and small are all to concern the two dukes; great affairs are to be decided with Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi;

sentences.zh: 若有軍旅，悉委慶之；

translations.literal: if there are military campaigns, all are to be entrusted to Qingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: if there are military campaigns, all are to be entrusted to Qingzhi;

sentences.zh: 尚書中事，委僕射顏師伯；

translations.literal: affairs within the Secretariat are to be entrusted to Vice Director Yan Shibo;
translations.idiomatic: affairs within the Secretariat are to be entrusted to Vice Director Yan Shibo;

sentences.zh: 外臨所統，委領軍將軍王玄謨。」

translations.literal: external command of what is overseen is to be entrusted to Director of the Palace Guards Wang Xuanmo."
translations.idiomatic: external command is to be entrusted to Director of the Palace Guards Wang Xuanmo."

sentences.zh: 是日，太子即皇帝位，年十六。

translations.literal: That day the crown prince took the imperial throne; he was sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: That day the crown prince took the throne; he was sixteen.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書蔡興宗親奉璽綬，太子受之，傲惰無戚容。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cai Xingzong personally presented the seal and cord; the crown prince received them with arrogance and indolence, without a sorrowful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cai Xingzong personally presented the seal and cord; the crown prince received them with arrogance and indolence, without a sorrowful countenance.

sentences.zh: 興宗出，告人曰：「昔魯昭不戚，叔孫知其不終。

translations.literal: Xingzong went out and told others, "In old times Duke Zhao of Lu showed no sorrow, and Shusun knew he would not end well.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong went out and told others, "In old times Duke Zhao of Lu showed no sorrow, and Shusun knew he would not end well.

sentences.zh: 家國之禍，其在此乎！」

translations.literal: The calamity of house and state — is it here!"
translations.idiomatic: The calamity of house and state — is it here!"

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔復以太宰義恭錄尚書事，柳元景加開府儀同三司，領丹陽尹，解南兗州。

translations.literal: On jiazi, an edict again made Grand Tutor Yigong recorder of Secretariat affairs; Liu Yuanjing was given Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, made Danyang Prefect, and relieved of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, an edict again made Grand Tutor Liu Yigong recorder of Secretariat affairs; Liu Yuanjing was given Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, appointed Danyang Prefect, and relieved of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁亥，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dinghai, the Wei ruler went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dinghai, the Northern Wei emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己亥，以晉安王子勳為江州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jihai, Prince Zixun of Jin'an was made Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jihai, Prince Zixun of Jin'an was appointed Governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 柔然處羅可汗卒，子予成立，號曰受羅部真可汗，改元永康。

translations.literal: Rouran Khan Chuluo died; his son Yucheng succeeded, taking the title Khan Shouluobuzhen and changing the era name to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran Khan Chuluo died; his son Yucheng succeeded, taking the title Khan Shouluobuzhen and changing the era name to Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 部真帥眾侵魏；

translations.literal: Buzhen led his host to invade Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Buzhen led his host to invade Northern Wei;

sentences.zh: 辛丑，魏北鎮遊軍擊破之。

translations.literal: on xinchou, Wei's northern garrison patrol troops defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: on xinchou, Northern Wei's northern garrison patrol troops defeated them.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏主如河西。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Wei ruler went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the Northern Wei emperor went to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 高車五部相聚祭天，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: The five divisions of the Gaoche gathered to sacrifice to Heaven; the multitude reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The five divisions of the Gaoche gathered to sacrifice to Heaven; the multitude reached tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 魏主親往臨視之，高車大喜。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler personally went to observe; the Gaoche were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor personally went to observe; the Gaoche were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 丙午，葬孝武皇帝於景寧陵，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Emperor Xiaowu was buried at Jingning Mausoleum; his temple name was Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Emperor Xiaowu was buried at Jingning Mausoleum; his temple name was Shizu.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager, and the empress as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager, and the empress as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，罷南北二馳道，及孝建以來所改制度，還依元嘉。

translations.literal: On yimao, the northern and southern expressways were abolished, and the institutions changed since Xiaojian were restored to follow Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the northern and southern expressways were abolished, and the institutions changed since the Xiaojian era were restored to follow the Yuanjia model.

sentences.zh: 尚書蔡興宗於都座慨然謂顏師伯曰：「先帝雖非盛德之主，要以道始終。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Cai Xingzong said with feeling at the capital seat to Yan Shibo, "The late emperor, though not a ruler of overflowing virtue, still observed the Way from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Director Cai Xingzong said with feeling at the capital seat to Yan Shibo, "The late emperor, though not a ruler of overflowing virtue, still observed the Way from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 三年無改，古典所貴。

translations.literal: Three years without change — this the ancient canon holds precious.
translations.idiomatic: Three years without change — this the ancient canon holds precious.

sentences.zh: 今殯宮始撤，山陵未遠，而凡諸制度興造，不論是非，一皆刊削，雖復禪代，亦不至爾。

translations.literal: Now the mourning palace has only just been withdrawn and the mountain tomb is not yet distant, yet every institution and construction, regardless of right or wrong, is entirely cut away — even at a transfer of the mandate it would not go this far.
translations.idiomatic: Now the mourning palace has only just been withdrawn and the mountain tomb is not yet distant, yet every institution and construction, regardless of merit, is entirely cut away — even at a transfer of the mandate it would not go this far.

sentences.zh: 天下有識，當以此窺人。」

translations.literal: Men of discernment in the realm will judge the man by this."
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment in the realm will judge the man by this."

sentences.zh: 太宰義恭素畏戴法興、巢尚之等，雖受遺輔政，而此身避事，由師伯不從。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yigong had long feared Dai Faxing, Chao Shangzhi, and others; though he received the testamentary charge to assist in government, he himself avoided affairs — because Shibo would not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Liu Yigong had long feared Dai Faxing, Chao Shangzhi, and others; though he received the testamentary charge to assist in government, he himself avoided affairs — because Shibo would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 是政歸近習。

translations.literal: Thus government power returned to those near and familiar.
translations.idiomatic: Thus government power returned to the emperor's intimates.

sentences.zh: 法興等專制朝權，威德近遠，詔敕皆出其手；

translations.literal: Faxing and others monopolized court power; their authority and virtue reached near and far; edicts and orders all came from their hands;
translations.idiomatic: Faxing and others monopolized court power; their authority reached near and far; edicts and orders all came from their hands;

sentences.zh: 尚書事無大小，鹹取決焉，義恭與顏師伯但守空名而已。

translations.literal: Secretariat affairs great and small were all decided there; Yigong and Yan Shibo merely kept empty titles.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat affairs great and small were all decided there; Yigong and Yan Shibo merely kept empty titles.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗自以職管銓衡，每至上朝，輒為義恭陳登賢進士之意，又箴規得失，博論朝政。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong, considering his office governed the scales of selection, at every court audience set forth to Yigong his intent to elevate the worthy and advance scholars, and also admonished on right and wrong, broadly discussing court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong, considering his office governed appointments, at every court audience set forth to Yigong his intent to elevate the worthy and advance scholars, and also admonished on right and wrong, broadly discussing court affairs.

sentences.zh: 義恭性恇撓，阿順法興，恆慮失旨，聞興宗言，輒戰懼無答，興宗每奏選事，法興、尚之等輒點定國回換，僅有在者。

translations.literal: Yigong's nature was timid and yielding; he flattered and followed Faxing and constantly feared missing the intent; hearing Xingzong's words, he would tremble in fear without reply; whenever Xingzong memorialized on selection matters, Faxing, Shangzhi, and others would mark and fix, sending back and exchanging — only a few remained in place.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was timid by nature; he flattered Faxing and constantly feared missing the mark; hearing Xingzong's words, he would tremble without reply; whenever Xingzong memorialized on appointments, Faxing, Shangzhi, and others would revise and exchange names — only a few remained.

sentences.zh: 興宗於朝堂謂義恭、師伯曰：「主上諒暗，不親萬機；

translations.literal: Xingzong said in the court hall to Yigong and Shibo, "The lord is in deep mourning and does not personally handle the myriad affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said in the court hall to Yigong and Shibo, "The lord is in deep mourning and does not personally handle state affairs;

sentences.zh: 而選舉密事，多被刪改，復非公筆，亦不知是何天子意！」

translations.literal: yet confidential selection matters are mostly deleted and altered — and they are not even in your own hand; who knows what Son of Heaven's intent this is!"
translations.idiomatic: yet confidential appointment matters are mostly deleted and altered — and they are not even in your own hand; who knows whose intent this is!"

sentences.zh: 數與義恭等爭選事，往復論執。

translations.literal: He repeatedly contended with Yigong and others over selection matters, arguing back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly contended with Yigong and others over appointments, arguing back and forth.

sentences.zh: 義恭、法興皆惡之。

translations.literal: Yigong and Faxing both hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong and Faxing both hated him.

sentences.zh: 左遷興宗新昌太守；

translations.literal: Xingzong was demoted to Administrator of Xinchang;
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong was demoted to Administrator of Xinchang;

sentences.zh: 既而以其人望，復留之建康。

translations.literal: then because of his public esteem, he was again kept at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: then because of his public esteem, he was again kept at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，追立何妃曰獻皇后。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Consort He was posthumously established as Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Consort He was posthumously established as Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，新安王子鸞解領司徒。

translations.literal: On yichou, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an relinquished his concurrent post as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an relinquished his concurrent post as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 戴法興等惡王玄謨剛嚴，八月，丁卯，以玄謨為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Dai Faxing and others hated Wang Xuanmo's stern severity; in the eighth month, on dingmao, Xuanmo was made Governor of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing and others hated Wang Xuanmo's stern severity; in the eighth month, on dingmao, Xuanmo was appointed Governor of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 王太后疾篤，使呼廢帝。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wang was gravely ill and sent to summon the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wang was gravely ill and sent to summon the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「病人間多鬼，那可往！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Among the sick there are many ghosts — how can one go there!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The sickroom is full of ghosts — how can I go there!"

sentences.zh: 太后怒，謂侍者：「取刀來，剖我腹，那得生寧馨兒！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager was enraged and said to her attendants, "Bring a knife — I will cut open my belly; how did I give birth to this precious child!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was enraged and said to her attendants, "Bring a knife — I will cut open my belly; how did I give birth to this precious child!"

sentences.zh: 己丑，太后殂。

translations.literal: On jichou, the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛丑，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinchou, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinchou, the Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以尚書左僕射劉遵考為特進、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On guimao, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Zunkao was made Special Advance and Right Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Left Vice Director Liu Zunkao was appointed Special Advance and Right Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，葬文穆皇后於景寧陵。

translations.literal: On yimao, Empress Wenmu was buried at Jingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Empress Wenmu was buried at Jingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，壬辰，以王畿諸郡為揚州，以揚州為東揚州。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on renchen, the commanderies of the royal domain were made Yangzhou, and Yangzhou was made Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the twelfth month, on renchen, the commanderies of the royal domain were made Yangzhou, and Yangzhou was renamed Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以豫章王子尚為司徒、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On guisi, Prince Zishang of Yuzhang was made Minister of Education and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Prince Zishang of Yuzhang was appointed Minister of Education and Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，青州移治東陽。

translations.literal: This year, Qingzhou moved its seat to Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: This year, Qingzhou moved its seat to Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 宋之境內，凡有州二十二，郡二百七十四，縣千二百九十九，戶九十四萬有奇。

translations.literal: Within Song's borders there were in all twenty-two provinces, two hundred seventy-four commanderies, one thousand two hundred ninety-nine counties, and households numbering nine hundred forty thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Within Song's borders there were twenty-two provinces, two hundred seventy-four commanderies, one thousand two hundred ninety-nine counties, and roughly nine hundred forty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 東方諸郡連歲旱，饑，米一升錢數百，建康亦至百餘錢，餓死者什六七。

translations.literal: The eastern commanderies suffered drought year after year and famine; rice cost several hundred cash per sheng, and even at Jiankang it reached more than a hundred — of those who starved, six or seven in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern commanderies suffered drought year after year and famine; rice cost several hundred cash per sheng, and even at Jiankang more than a hundred — six or seven in ten of those who starved died.
